value.zh: 又言：「燕、趙之民，椎牛裹糧，首先歸命。
value.en: He also wrote: "The people of Yan and Zhao slaughtered cattle and packed provisions to be the first to submit to the new dynasty.
value.literal: He also said: "The people of Yan and Zhao slaughtered cattle and wrapped grain, being the first to submit.

value.zh: 此漢高之關中，光武之河內也。
value.en: They were to the Qing what Guanzhong had been to Gaozu of Han and Henei to Emperor Guangwu.
value.literal: This is like Gaozu of Han's Guanzhong and Guangwu's Henei.

value.zh: 今天下初定，屢奉詔蠲賦，而畿輔未霑實惠，宜切責奉行之吏，彰信於民。」
value.en: Now that the realm is newly pacified, repeated edicts have remitted taxes, yet the capital districts have not felt the real benefit. Officials charged with carrying out these orders should be held strictly accountable so that the government's word is made credible to the people."
value.literal: Now that the realm is newly settled, decrees for tax remission have been issued repeatedly, yet the capital region has not received the real benefit; the officials charged with implementation should be sternly held accountable, so that trust is made clear to the people."

value.zh: 俱報聞。
value.en: All of these proposals were noted by the throne.
value.literal: All were acknowledged.

value.zh: 五十二年，與千叟宴，賜賚有加。
value.en: In the fifty-second year he attended the banquet for elders of a thousand years and received especially generous gifts.
value.literal: In the fifty-second year he attended the banquet for a thousand elders and received especially generous gifts.

value.zh: 頃之，以病乞休，溫旨慰留。
value.en: Before long he asked to retire on grounds of illness; a warm edict comforted him and urged him to stay.
value.literal: Before long, on account of illness he requested retirement; a warm edict comforted him and asked him to remain.

value.zh: 越二年，復以為請，且言母喪未葬，許給假二年，賜詩寵行。
value.en: Two years later he asked again, adding that his mother's burial was still unfinished. He was granted two years' leave and sent off with an imperial poem.
value.literal: Two years later he again made the request, and also said his mother's funeral had not yet been conducted; he was granted two years' leave and received an imperial poem honoring his departure.

value.zh: 五十六年，還朝，累疏乞罷，上以大學士王掞方在告，暫止之。
value.en: In the fifty-sixth year he returned to court and repeatedly asked to be dismissed, but the emperor held off because Grand Secretary Wang Yan was already away on leave.
value.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he returned to court, repeatedly memorialized asking to be dismissed, and the emperor temporarily stopped this because Grand Secretary Wang Yan was already on leave.

value.zh: 五十七年，卒，年七十七，遣恆親王允祺奠醊，賜金千兩，諡文貞。
value.en: In the fifty-seventh year he died at seventy-seven. Prince Heng Yinqi was sent to offer libations, one thousand taels of silver were granted, and he was posthumously honored as Wen Zhen.
value.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died at the age of seventy-seven; Prince Heng Yinqi was sent to offer libations, one thousand taels of silver were granted, and he was posthumously given the honorific Wen Zhen.

value.zh: 使工部尚書徐元夢護其喪歸，复諭閣臣：「李光地謹慎清勤，始終一節，學問淵博。
value.en: Minister of Works Xu Yuanmeng was sent to escort the bier home, and the emperor again told the grand secretaries, "Li Guangdi was careful, pure, and diligent, unwavering to the end, and his learning was broad and deep.
value.literal: Minister of Works Xu Yuanmeng was sent to escort the funeral home, and the emperor again instructed the grand secretaries: "Li Guangdi was careful, pure, and diligent, consistent from beginning to end, and his learning was broad and deep.

value.zh: 朕知之最真，知朕亦無過光地者！」
value.en: I know this better than anyone, and among those who truly know me, none surpasses Li Guangdi!"
value.literal: I know this most truly, and among those who know me none surpasses Guangdi!

value.zh: 雍正初，贈太子太傅，祀賢良祠。
value.en: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and entered the Shrine of Worthy Ministers.
value.literal: In the early Yongzheng reign he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Ministers.

value.zh: 太祖三
value.en: Annals of Taizu, continued.
value.literal: Taizu III.

value.zh: 冬十月甲申，幸迎春苑，登汴隄觀戰艦東下。
value.en: In the tenth month of winter, on jiashen, he went to Welcome Spring Garden, climbed the Bian dike, and watched the fleet head downstream.
value.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiashen, he visited Welcome Spring Garden, ascended the Bian embankment, and watched the warships sail east.

value.zh: 丙戌，又幸迎春苑，登汴隄觀諸軍習戰，遂幸東水門，發戰櫂東下。
value.en: On bingxu he returned to Welcome Spring Garden, reviewed troop exercises from the dike, then went to East Water Gate and launched the battle fleet eastward.
value.literal: On bingxu, he again visited Welcome Spring Garden, ascended the Bian embankment to watch the various armies drill, then visited East Water Gate and sent the war fleet east.

value.zh: 江南進絹數萬，御衣、金帶、器用數百事。
value.en: Southern Tang sent tens of thousands in silk, court robes, gold belts, and several hundred pieces of ritual ware.
value.literal: Jiangnan presented tens of thousands in silk, imperial robes, gold belts, and vessels numbering in the hundreds.

value.zh: 壬辰，曹彬等將舟師、步騎發江陵，水陸並進。
value.en: On renchen Cao Bin's river and land columns left Jiangling in combined advance.
value.literal: On renchen, Cao Bin and the others led the fleet and infantry and cavalry to depart from Jiangling, advancing by land and water together.

value.zh: 丁酉，命吳越王錢俶為昇州東南行營招撫制置使。
value.en: On dingyou King Qian Chu of Wuyue was named pacification commissioner on the southeastern front against Shengzhou.
value.literal: On dingyou, Wuyue king Qian Chu was made pacification and disposition commissioner of the Southeast Route Army for Shengzhou.

value.zh: 己亥，曹彬收下峽口，獲指揮使王仁震、王宴、錢興。
value.en: On jihai Cao Bin seized Xiakou and took commanders Wang Renzhen, Wang Yan, and Qian Xing prisoner.
value.literal: On jihai, Cao Bin took Xiakou and captured commanders Wang Renzhen, Wang Yan, and Qian Xing.

value.zh: 高宗受命中興全功至德聖神武文昭仁憲孝皇帝，諱構，字德基，徽宗第九子，母曰顯仁皇后韋氏。
value.en: Gaozong—Received-the-Mandate, Restored-the-Dynasty, Full-Merit, Utmost-Virtue, Sage, Divine, Martial, Literary, Illustrious, Benevolent, Constitutional, Filial—taboo Gou, style Deji, Huizong’s ninth son, born of Empress Xianren Wei.
value.literal: Gaozong, the emperor who received the mandate, restored the dynasty, accomplished full merit, utmost virtue, sage, divine, martial, literary, illustrious, benevolent, constitutional, and filial—taboo name Gou, courtesy name Deji—was Huizong’s ninth son; his mother was Empress Xianren of the Wei clan.

value.zh: 大觀元年五月乙巳生東京之大內，赤光照室。
value.en: Daguan 1, fifth month, yisi: born in Dongjing’s inner palace; red light washed the room.
value.literal: Daguan year 1, fifth month, day yisi: he was born in the great inner palace at Dongjing; red light filled the chamber.

value.zh: 八月丁丑，賜名，授定武軍節度使、檢校太尉，封蜀國公。
value.en: Eighth month, dingchou: named and made Dingwu commissioner, Grand General, Duke of Shu.
value.literal: Eighth month, day dingchou: a name was granted; he was made military commissioner of Dingwu army, checked Grand General, and enfeoffed Duke of Shu.

value.zh: 二年正月庚申，封廣平郡王。
value.en: In the second year, first month, gengshen: Prince of Guangping.
value.literal: In the second year, first month, day gengshen: he was advanced to Prince of Guangping commandery.

value.zh: 宣和三年十二月壬子，進封康王。
value.en: Xuanhe 3, twelfth month, renzi: Prince of Kang.
value.literal: Xuanhe year 3, twelfth month, day renzi: he was advanced to Prince of Kang.

value.zh: 資性朗悟，博學強記，讀書日誦千餘言，挽弓至一石五鬥。
value.en: Bright of wit, deep in learning and memory, he recited a thousand characters a day and drew the bow to one stone five pecks.
value.literal: By nature bright and quick, he studied widely and remembered strongly, reciting more than a thousand characters a day in reading, and drawing the bow to one stone five pecks.

value.zh: 宣和四年，始冠，出就外第。
value.en: Xuanhe 4: capped, he moved to an outer mansion.
value.literal: Xuanhe year 4: he received the capping rite and went out to an outer residence.

value.zh: 九月己丑，建州軍校張員等作亂，執守臣張動，轉運副使毛奎、判官曹仔為所殺，嬰城自守。
value.en: Ninth month, jichou: Jianzhou soldiers under Zhang Yuan mutinied, seized Zhang Dong, killed Mao Kui and Cao Zai, and held the city.
value.literal: Ninth month, day jichou: Jianzhou soldiers under Zhang Yuan and others mutinied, seized defender Zhang Dong, and killed transport vice commissioner Mao Kui and judge Cao Zai; they held the city in defense.

value.zh: 范瓊捕斬李孝忠於復州。
value.en: Fan Qiong captured and beheaded Li Xiaozhong at Fuzhou.
value.literal: Fan Qiong captured and beheaded Li Xiaozhong at Fuzhou.

value.zh: 壬辰，以金人犯河陽、汜水，詔擇日巡幸淮甸。
value.en: On renchen, with Jin attacking Heyang and Sishui, an edict chose a day to tour the Huai region.
value.literal: Day renchen: because the Jin attacked Heyang and Sishui, an edict chose a day to tour the Huai region.

value.zh: 鑄建炎通寶錢。
value.en: Jianyan universal treasure cash was cast.
value.literal: Jianyan universal treasure cash was cast.

value.zh: 命淮、浙沿海諸州增修城壁，招訓民兵，以備海道。
value.en: Huai and Zhe coastal prefectures were ordered to heighten walls, train militia, and guard the sea routes.
value.literal: Coastal prefectures of Huai and Zhe were ordered to heighten walls, recruit and train militia, and prepare the sea routes.

value.zh: 甲午，命揚州守臣呂頤浩繕修城池。
value.en: On jiawu, Yangzhou defender Lü Yihao was ordered to repair the walls.
value.literal: Day jiawu: Yangzhou defender Lü Yihao was ordered to repair walls.

value.zh: 宗澤往河北視師，七日還。
value.en: Zong Ze went to Hebei to inspect the armies and returned in seven days.
value.literal: Zong Ze went to Hebei to inspect the armies and returned in seven days.

value.zh: 是夜，辛道宗兵潰於嘉興縣。
value.en: That night Xin Daozong’s troops collapsed at Jiaxing.
value.literal: That night Xin Daozong’s troops collapsed at Jiaxing county.

value.zh: 丁酉，詔荊襄、關陝、江淮皆備巡幸。
value.en: On dingyou, Jing–Xiang, Guan–Shaan, and Jiang–Huai were ordered to prepare for the imperial progress.
value.literal: Day dingyou: an edict ordered Jing–Xiang, Guan–Shaan, and Jiang–Huai all to prepare for the imperial progress.

value.zh: 戊戌，罷買馬。
value.en: On wuxu, horse purchases were abolished.
value.literal: Day wuxu: horse purchases were abolished.

value.zh: 己亥，以子旉為檢校少保、集慶軍節度使，封魏國公。
value.en: On jihai, the son Fang was made acting Junior Guardian and Jiqing military commissioner and enfeoffed Duke of Wei.
value.literal: Day jihai: the son Fang was made acting Junior Guardian and Jiqing military commissioner and enfeoffed Duke of Wei.

value.zh: 詔內外官司參用嘉祐、元豐敕，以俟新書。
value.en: Inner and outer offices were ordered to apply Jiayou and Yuanfeng statutes provisionally pending new codes.
value.literal: An edict ordered inner and outer offices to apply provisionally the Jiayou and Yuanfeng statutes pending new books.

value.zh: 庚子，二帝徙居霫郡。
value.en: On gengzi, the two emperors were moved to Xi commandery.
value.literal: Day gengzi: the two emperors were moved to Xi commandery.

value.zh: 辛丑，陳通劫提點刑獄周格營，殺格，執提點刑獄高士曈。
value.en: On xinchou, Chen Tong raided judicial intendant Zhou Ge’s camp, killed Ge, and seized Gao Shitan.
value.literal: Day xinchou: Chen Tong raided judicial intendant Zhou Ge’s camp, killed Ge, and seized judicial intendant Gao Shitan.

value.zh: 壬寅，遣徽猷閣待制孟忠厚迎奉太廟神主赴揚州。
value.en: On renyin, Imperial Writings attendant Meng Zhonghou was sent to escort the ancestral tablets to Yangzhou.
value.literal: Day renyin: Imperial Writings Hall attendant Meng Zhonghou was sent to escort the ancestral temple tablets to Yangzhou.

value.zh: 以直秘閣王圭為招撫判官，代張所，尋責所廣南安置。
value.en: Direct Secretariat academician Wang Gui replaced Zhang Suo as pacification judge; soon Suo was exiled to the far south.
value.literal: Direct Secretariat academician Wang Gui was made pacification judge, replacing Zhang Suo; soon Suo was blamed and placed in the far south.

value.zh: 乙巳，宗澤表請車駕還闕。
value.en: On yisi, Zong Ze memorialized asking the throne to return to the capital.
value.literal: Day yisi: Zong Ze memorialized asking the imperial carriage to return to the capital.

value.zh: 戊申，河北招撫司都統制王彥渡河擊金人，破之，復新鄉縣。
value.en: On wushen, Hebei pacification overall controller Wang Yan crossed the river, defeated the Jin, and recovered Xinxiang.
value.literal: Day wushen: Hebei pacification headquarters overall controller Wang Yan crossed the river, defeated the Jin, and recovered Xinxiang county.

value.zh: 己酉，以諜報金人欲犯江、浙，詔暫駐淮甸捍禦，稍定即還京闕。
value.en: On jiyou, hearing the Jin meant to attack Jiang and Zhe, an edict halted temporarily in the Huai region for defense and promised return to the capital once settled.
value.literal: Day jiyou: on intelligence that the Jin meant to attack Jiang and Zhe, an edict ordered a temporary halt in the Huai region for defense and return to the capital once settled.

value.zh: 募民入貲授官。
value.en: Commoners were recruited to buy office with wealth.
value.literal: The people were recruited to buy office with wealth.

value.zh: 軍賊趙萬入常州，執守臣何袞。
value.en: Army-bandit Zhao Wan entered Changzhou and seized defender He Gun.
value.literal: Army-bandit Zhao Wan entered Changzhou and seized defender He Gun.

value.zh: 罷諸路經制招撫使。
value.en: Circuit commissioner-generals and pacification commissioners were abolished.
value.literal: Circuit commissioner-generals and pacification commissioners were abolished.

value.zh: 庚戌，始通當三大錢於淮、浙、荊湖諸路。
value.en: On gengxu, the three-large cash was first circulated in Huai, Zhe, and Jing–lake circuits.
value.literal: Day gengxu: the three-large cash was first circulated in Huai, Zhe, and Jing–lake circuits.

value.zh: 壬子，命湖南撫諭官馬伸持詔賜張邦昌死於潭州，並誅王時雍。
value.en: On renzi, Hunan reassurance commissioner Ma Shen was ordered to grant Zhang Bangchang death at Tanzhou and execute Wang Shiyong.
value.literal: Day renzi: Hunan reassurance commissioner Ma Shen was ordered to carry an edict granting Zhang Bangchang death at Tanzhou and also to execute Wang Shiyong.

value.zh: 癸丑，詔有敢妄議惑眾沮巡幸者，許告而罪之，不告者斬。
value.en: On guichou, whoever rashly debated to obstruct the progress might be reported and punished; non-reporters were to be beheaded.
value.literal: Day guichou: an edict—whoever rashly debated and misled the masses to obstruct the progress might be reported and punished; those who did not report were to be beheaded.

value.zh: 乙卯，王彥及金人戰，敗績，奔太行山聚眾，其裨將岳飛引其部曲自為一軍。
value.en: On yimao, Wang Yan fought the Jin, was defeated, fled to the Taihang to gather troops; lieutenant Yue Fei led his detachment separately.
value.literal: Day yimao: Wang Yan fought the Jin and was defeated; he fled to the Taihang Mountains to gather troops; his lieutenant Yue Fei led his own detachment as a separate army.

value.zh: 趙萬陷鎮江府，守臣趙子崧棄城渡江，保瓜洲。
value.en: Zhao Wan took Zhenjiang; Zhao Zisong abandoned the city, crossed the river, and held Guazhou.
value.literal: Zhao Wan took Zhenjiang prefecture; defender Zhao Zisong abandoned the city, crossed the river, and held Guazhou.

value.zh: 是秋，金人分兵據兩河州縣，惟中山、慶源府、保、莫、邢洺、冀、磁、絳、相州久之乃陷。
value.en: That autumn Jin divided troops to hold Two He prefectures; only Zhongshan, Qingyuan, Bao, Mo, Xing, Mozhou, Ji, Ci, Jiang, and Xiang fell after long resistance.
value.literal: That autumn the Jin divided troops to hold Two He prefectures and counties; only Zhongshan, Qingyuan prefecture, Bao, Mo, Xing, Mo prefecture, Ji, Ci, Jiang, and Xiang fell only after long resistance.

value.zh: 三十一年春正月甲戌朔，以日食，不受朝。
value.en: Year 31, spring, jiaxu new moon: Gaozong canceled audience for the eclipse.
value.literal: Thirty-first year, spring, first month, day jiaxu new moon: because of a solar eclipse, court audience was not held.

value.zh: 丁丑，雷。
value.en: On dingchou, thunder rolled.
value.literal: Day dingchou: thunder.

value.zh: 丁亥，免湖州增丁所輸絹。
value.en: On dinghai, Huzhou was freed from added-household silk levies.
value.literal: Day dinghai: the silk paid by Huzhou for added registered households was remitted.

value.zh: 夜，風雷雨雪交作。
value.en: That night wind, thunder, snow, and rain came together.
value.literal: At night, wind, thunder, snow, and rain struck together.

value.zh: 辛卯，詔江、浙官民戶均輸和市絁帛。
value.en: On xinmao, Jiang and Zhe were told to share silk transport and market purchases equally among official and common households.
value.literal: Day xinmao: an edict ordered official and common households of Jiang and Zhe to share equally in transport and market purchase of silk.

value.zh: 壬辰，劉寶落節鉞、福建路居住。
value.en: On renchen, Liu Bao lost his command tally and was sent to live on the Fujian circuit.
value.literal: Day renchen: Liu Bao was stripped of his command tally and made to reside on the Fujian circuit.

value.zh: 丙申，大雨雪，給三衙衛士、行在貧民錢及薪炭，命常平振給輔郡細民，諸路監司決獄。
value.en: On bingchen, heavy snow brought cash and charcoal to palace guards and capital poor; Ever-Normal stores fed nearby counties; commissioners judged cases.
value.literal: Day bingchen: in great rain and snow, money and fuel were given to the Three Yamaz guards and poor people at the mobile court; the Ever-Normal Granaries were ordered to relieve needy folk in auxiliary commanderies; circuit commissioners were to decide cases.

value.zh: 己亥，放張浚、胡銓自便。
value.en: On jihai, Zhang Jun and Hu Quan were freed to their own devices.
value.literal: Day jihai: Zhang Jun and Hu Quan were released to go as they pleased.

value.zh: 庚子，禁淮南拘籍戶馬。
value.en: On gengzi, Huainan could no longer seize and register civilian horses.
value.literal: Day gengzi: Huainan was forbidden to seize and register household horses.

value.zh: 十一月己巳朔，邵宏淵遣統領崔皋及金人戰於定山，敗之。
value.en: Eleventh month, jisi new moon: Shao Hongyuan's Cui Gao beat the Jin at Dingshan.
value.literal: Eleventh month, day jisi new moon: Shao Hongyuan sent commander Cui Gao to fight the Jin at Dingshan and defeated them.

value.zh: 任天錫復虢州，守將蕭信遁去。
value.en: Ren Tiansi retook Guozhou; Xiao Xin fled.
value.literal: Ren Tiansi recovered Guozhou; the Jin prefect Xiao Xin fled.

value.zh: 庚午，通州守臣崔邦弼棄城去。
value.en: On gengwu, Tongzhou's Cui Bangbi abandoned his post.
value.literal: Day gengwu: Tongzhou prefect Cui Bangbi abandoned the city and left.

value.zh: 辛未，成閔引兵發應城縣，援淮西。
value.en: On xinwei, Cheng Min marched from Yingcheng to aid Huai West.
value.literal: Day xinwei: Cheng Min led troops from Yingcheng county to aid Huai West.

value.zh: 遣權吏部侍郎汪應辰詣浙東措置海道。
value.en: Wang Yingchen was sent to organize the Zhe East sea route.
value.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Personnel Wang Yingchen was sent to arrange the sea route in Zhe East.

value.zh: 壬申，以張浚判建康府。
value.en: On renshen, Zhang Jun was assigned Jiankang.
value.literal: Day renshen: Zhang Jun was made to judge Jiankang prefecture.

value.zh: 召王權赴行在，以李顯忠代將。
value.en: Wang Quan was recalled; Li Xianzhong took his command.
value.literal: Wang Quan was summoned to the mobile court; Li Xianzhong replaced him in command.

value.zh: 邵宏淵為池州都統制。
value.en: Shao Hongyuan became Chizhou overall commander.
value.literal: Shao Hongyuan was made Chizhou overall commander.

value.zh: 金人犯瓜州，鎮江中軍統制劉汜戰敗走，權都統制李橫亦遁。
value.en: The Jin hit Guazhou; Liu Si fled in defeat and Li Heng with him.
value.literal: Jin troops attacked Guazhou; Zhenjiang central-army controller Liu Si was defeated and fled; acting overall commander Li Heng also fled.

value.zh: 金人鐵騎奄至江上，統制魏俊、王方死之。
value.en: Jin iron cavalry swept to the riverbank; Wei Jun and Wang Fang fell.
value.literal: Jin iron cavalry suddenly reached the river; controllers Wei Jun and Wang Fang died.

value.zh: 葉義問惶怖欲退走，復趨建康。
value.en: Ye Yiwen nearly fled in panic, then rushed to Jiankang.
value.literal: Ye Yiwen in panic wished to withdraw but then hurried to Jiankang.

value.zh: 金人游騎至無為軍，守臣韓髦棄城走。
value.en: Jin raiders reached Wuwei; Han Mao fled.
value.literal: Jin raiders reached Wuwei Army; prefect Han Mao abandoned the city and fled.

value.zh: 癸酉，淮甯府民陳亨祖執同知完顏耶魯，以其城來歸。
value.en: On guiyou, Chen Hengzu of Huaining seized Wanyan Yelu and surrendered the city.
value.literal: Day guiyou: Huaining prefecture commoner Chen Hengzu seized Vice Prefect Wanyan Yelu and brought the city in.

value.zh: 趙撙引兵去，蔡州復陷。
value.en: Zhao Zan withdrew and Caizhou fell again.
value.literal: Zhao Zan led troops away; Caizhou again fell.

value.zh: 甲戌，池州統制官崔定等復入無為軍。
value.en: On jiaxu, Cui Ding of Chizhou re-entered Wuwei Army.
value.literal: Day jiaxu: Chizhou controller Cui Ding and others re-entered Wuwei Army.

value.zh: 乙亥，金主亮臨江築壇，刑馬祭天，期以翌日南渡。
value.en: On yihai, Hailing sacrificed a horse by the river and vowed to cross the next day.
value.literal: Day yihai: the Jin ruler Hailing built an altar by the river, slaughtered a horse to sacrifice to Heaven, and set the next day to cross south.

value.zh: 丙子，虞允文督建康諸軍統制官張振、王琪、時俊、戴皋等以舟師拒金主亮於東採石，戰勝，卻之。
value.en: On bingzi, Yu Yunwen's fleet met Hailing at East Caishi, won, and drove him back.
value.literal: Day bingzi: Yu Yunwen directed Jiankang fleet controllers Zhang Zhen, Wang Qi, Shi Jun, and Dai Gao and others with warships to meet Hailing at East Caishi, fought, won, and drove him back.

value.zh: 崔定復巢縣，任天錫復上津、商洛二縣。
value.en: Cui Ding retook Chao; Ren Tiansi retook Shangjin and Shangluo.
value.literal: Cui Ding recovered Chao county; Ren Tiansi recovered Shangjin and Shangluo counties.

value.zh: 丁丑，虞允文遣水軍統制盛新以舟師擊金人于楊林河口，又敗之。
value.en: On dingchou, Yu Yunwen's Sheng Xin beat the Jin again at Yanglin mouth.
value.literal: Day dingchou: Yu Yunwen sent naval controller Sheng Xin with warships to strike the Jin at Yanglin River mouth and again defeated them.

value.zh: 金主亮焚其舟而去。
value.en: Hailing burned his boats and withdrew.
value.literal: The Jin ruler Hailing burned his boats and left.

value.zh: 戊寅，王彥遣將楊堅復欒川縣。
value.en: On wuyin, Wang Yan's Yang Jian retook Luanchuan.
value.literal: Day wuyin: Wang Yan sent General Yang Jian to recover Luanchuan county.

value.zh: 己卯，以湯思退為行宮留守。
value.en: On jimao, Tang Situi was made mobile-court resident.
value.literal: Day jimao: Tang Situi was made mobile-court resident.

value.zh: 虛恨蠻犯嘉州籠蓬堡，官軍大敗，副將鄭祥等為所殺。
value.en: The Xuhuaiman struck Longpeng fort in Jiazhou; government troops were routed and deputy commander Zheng Xiang and others were killed.
value.literal: The Xuhuaiman attacked Jiazhou's Longpeng fort; government troops were badly beaten and deputy commander Zheng Xiang and others were killed.

value.zh: 庚辰，金主亮引軍趨淮東。
value.en: On gengchen, Jin Emperor Hailing marched toward Huai east.
value.literal: Day gengchen: the Jin ruler Hailing led his army toward Huai east.

value.zh: 癸未，吳璘病，自仙人原還興州，留姚仲節制軍事，虞允文自採石率李捧一軍及戈船如鎮江備敵。
value.en: On guimao, Wu Lin fell ill, left Xianrenyuan for Xing, put Yao Zhong in charge of the army, and Yu Yunwen from Caishi sent Li Peng's force and war junks to Zhenjiang.
value.literal: Day guimao: Wu Lin fell ill, returned from Xianrenyuan to Xing prefecture, left Yao Zhong to control the army, and Yu Yunwen from Caishi led Li Peng's army and war junks to Zhenjiang against the enemy.

value.zh: 甲申，贈姚興、魏俊、王方官。
value.en: On jiashen, Yao Xing, Wei Jun, and Wang Fang received posthumous enfeoffment.
value.literal: Day jiashen: Yao Xing, Wei Jun, and Wang Fang were posthumously enfeoffed.

value.zh: 金主亮至揚州。
value.en: Jin Emperor Hailing reached Yangzhou.
value.literal: The Jin ruler Hailing reached Yangzhou.

value.zh: 乙酉，貸劉汜死、英州編管。
value.en: On yiyou, Liu Si was spared execution and banished to Ying supervision.
value.literal: Day yiyou: Liu Si was spared death and banished to registered supervision at Ying prefecture.

value.zh: 江州統制李貴、忠義首領孟俊復順昌府，金州將邢進復華州。
value.en: Jiangzhou commander Li Gui and loyalist Meng Jun retook Shunchang; Jin officer Xing Jin retook Hua prefecture.
value.literal: Jiangzhou overall commander Li Gui and loyalist leader Meng Jun recovered Shunchang prefecture; Jin prefecture commander Xing Jin recovered Hua prefecture.

value.zh: 丙戌，賜戰士帛，給其家薪炭。
value.en: On bingxu, warriors received silk grants and their families were given fuel.
value.literal: Day bingxu: silk was granted to fighting men and fuel given their families.

value.zh: 任天錫復陝州。
value.en: Ren Tiansi retook Shan prefecture.
value.literal: Ren Tiansi recovered Shan prefecture.

value.zh: 丁亥，劉錡以疾罷，以禦營宿衛中軍統制劉銳權鎮江都統制。
value.en: On dinghai, Liu Qi left office for illness; central-army controller Liu Rui became acting Zhenjiang commander.
value.literal: Day dinghai: Liu Qi was dismissed for illness; Imperial Guard central-army controller Liu Rui was made acting Zhenjiang overall commander.

value.zh: 成閔自京西還建康，遂如鎮江。
value.en: Cheng Min came back from Jing west to Jiankang and then to Zhenjiang.
value.literal: Cheng Min returned from Jing west to Jiankang and then went to Zhenjiang.

value.zh: 戊子，吳璘復力疾上仙人原。
value.en: On wuzi, Wu Lin dragged himself back to Xianrenyuan despite illness.
value.literal: Day wuzi: Wu Lin again forced himself up to Xianrenyuan despite illness.

value.zh: 己丑，王權貸死、瓊州編管。
value.en: On jichou, Wang Quan was spared execution and banished to Qiong supervision.
value.literal: Day jichou: Wang Quan was spared death and banished to registered supervision at Qiong prefecture.

value.zh: 李寶泛海南歸。
value.en: Li Bao returned by sea from the south.
value.literal: Li Bao sailed the sea south and returned.

value.zh: 金人復攻陝州，任天錫破走之。
value.en: The Jin struck Shan again; Ren Tiansi beat them back.
value.literal: The Jin again attacked Shan prefecture; Ren Tiansi routed and drove them off.

value.zh: 復犯襄陽，統制官李勝等拒卻之，復通化軍。
value.en: They struck Xiangyang again; controller Li Sheng and others drove them off and restored Tonghua army.
value.literal: They again attacked Xiangyang; controller Li Sheng and others repelled them and restored Tonghua army.

value.zh: 王彥遣將楊堅、黨清至西京長水縣及金人戰，敗之。
value.en: Wang Yan sent Yang Jian and Dang Qing to Changshui west of the Western Capital, fought the Jin, and won.
value.literal: Wang Yan sent generals Yang Jian and Dang Qing to Changshui county west of the Western Capital and fought the Jin, defeating them.

value.zh: 庚寅，復長水縣。
value.en: On gengyin, Changshui county was restored.
value.literal: Day gengyin: Changshui county was restored.

value.zh: 癸巳，以成閔為鎮江都統制、淮東制置使、京東西路河北東路淮北泗宿州招討使，李顯忠為淮西制置使、京畿河北西路淮北壽亳州招討使，吳拱為湖北京西制置使、京西北路招討使。
value.en: On guisi, Cheng Min became Zhenjiang commander, Huai east commissioner, and reconquest commissioner for Jing west and east, Hebei east, and Huai-north Si and Su; Li Xianzhong became Huai west commissioner and reconquest commissioner for Jingji, Hebei west, and Huai-north Shou and Bo; Wu Gong became Hubei–Jing west commissioner and Jing northwest reconquest commissioner.
value.literal: Day guisi: Cheng Min was made Zhenjiang overall commander, Huai east commissioner, and commissioner for pacification and reconquest of Jing west, Jing east, Hebei east, and north of the Huai including Si and Su prefectures; Li Xianzhong Huai west commissioner and commissioner for Jingji, Hebei west, and north of the Huai including Shou and Bo prefectures; Wu Gong Hubei and Jing west commissioner and commissioner for Jing northwest.

value.zh: 甲午，武钜遣鄉兵總轄杜隱等復嵩州。
value.en: On jiawu, Wu Ju's militia commander Du Yin and others retook Song prefecture.
value.literal: Day jiawu: Wu Ju sent militia commander Du Yin and others to recover Song prefecture.

value.zh: 乙未，金人陷泰州。
value.en: On yiwei, the Jin captured Taizhou.
value.literal: Day yiwei: the Jin took Taizhou.

value.zh: 是日，金人弑其主亮於揚州龜山寺。
value.en: That day the Jin killed Emperor Hailing at Guishan Temple in Yangzhou.
value.literal: That day the Jin slew their ruler Hailing at Guishan Temple in Yangzhou.

value.zh: 戊戌，金都督府遣人持檄詣鎮江軍中議和。
value.en: On wuxu, the Jin command sent envoys with a peace proclamation to the Zhenjiang army.
value.literal: Day wuxu: the Jin command headquarters sent men with a proclamation to the Zhenjiang army to discuss peace.

value.zh: 二月戊戌朔，罷借兩浙、江、淮坊場淨利錢。
value.en: Second month, wuxu new moon: borrowing against Zhe, Jiang, and Huai licensed-shop profits was ended.
value.literal: Second month, day wuxu new moon: borrowing against licensed-shop net profits in the two Zhe, Jiang, and Huai circuits was ended.

value.zh: 以虞允文為兵部尚書、川陝宣諭使，措置招軍市馬及與吳璘議事。
value.en: Yu Yunwen became Minister of War and Sichuan-Shaanxi commissioner to handle recruiting, horse buying, and affairs with Wu Lin.
value.literal: Yu Yunwen was made Minister of War and Sichuan-Shaanxi commissioner for pacification, to handle recruiting, horse purchase, and affairs with Wu Lin.

value.zh: 庚子，興州統領惠逢等復河州。
value.en: On gengzi, Xing controller Hui Feng and others retook He prefecture.
value.literal: Day gengzi: Xing prefecture controller Hui Feng and others recovered He prefecture.

value.zh: 振兩淮饑民。
value.en: Two-Huai famine victims were relieved.
value.literal: Famine victims in the two Huai were relieved.

value.zh: 壬寅，金人犯汝州，守將王宣逆戰，敗之。
value.en: On renyin, the Jin struck Ru; defender Wang Xuan met them and won.
value.literal: Day renyin: the Jin attacked Ru prefecture; defending commander Wang Xuan met them and defeated them.

value.zh: 癸卯，帝發建康。
value.en: On guimao, the emperor left Jiankang.
value.literal: Day guimao: the Emperor set out from Jiankang.

value.zh: 惠逢復積石軍，又克來羌城。
value.en: Hui Feng retook Jishi army and also captured Laicang city.
value.literal: Hui Feng recovered Jishi army and also took Laicang city.

value.zh: 丁未，劉錡薨。
value.en: On dingwei, Liu Qi died.
value.literal: Day dingwei: Liu Qi died.

value.zh: 己酉，王宣及金人再戰於汝州。
value.en: On jiyou, Wang Xuan and the Jin fought again at Ru.
value.literal: Day jiyou: Wang Xuan and the Jin fought again at Ru prefecture.

value.zh: 庚戌，金人全師來攻，宣敗績，棄去。
value.en: On gengxu, the Jin came in full strength; Xuan was routed and withdrew.
value.literal: Day gengxu: the Jin came in full force; Xuan was beaten and withdrew.

value.zh: 辛亥，金人復犯順昌府，孟新拒卻之，尋亦棄去。
value.en: On xinhai, the Jin struck Shunchang again; Meng Xin beat them back and soon withdrew too.
value.literal: Day xinhai: the Jin again attacked Shunchang prefecture; Meng Xin repelled them and soon withdrew as well.

value.zh: 壬子，賞蔡州功，趙撙等進官有差。
value.en: On renzi, Cai victors were rewarded; Zhao Zong and others were promoted by degrees.
value.literal: Day renzi: Cai prefecture merit was rewarded; Zhao Zong and others were advanced in rank by degrees.

value.zh: 乙卯，至臨安府。
value.en: On yimao, he reached Lin'an.
value.literal: Day yimao: he reached Lin'an prefecture.

value.zh: 興元都統制姚仲攻鞏州不下，退守甘穀城，遂引兵圍德順軍。
value.en: Xingyuan commander Yao Zhong failed to take Gong, fell back to Gangu city, and besieged Deshun army.
value.literal: Xingyuan overall commander Yao Zhong attacked Gong prefecture without success, fell back to Gangu city, and then led troops to besiege Deshun army.

value.zh: 丙辰，金人犯蔡州。
value.en: On bingchen, the Jin attacked Cai prefecture.
value.literal: Day bingchen: the Jin attacked Cai prefecture.

value.zh: 趙撙擊卻之。
value.en: Zhao Zong beat them back.
value.literal: Zhao Zong struck and drove them off.

value.zh: 戊午，復引兵來攻，撙又敗之，金兵遁去。
value.en: On wuwu, they returned; Zong defeated them again and the Jin fled.
value.literal: Day wuwu: they came again; Zong again defeated them and the Jin fled.

value.zh: 王彥遣將馬貴斷河中南橋，金兵來攻，貴戰敗之。
value.en: Wang Yan sent Ma Gui to cut the Yellow River's south bridge; the Jin attacked and Gui defeated them.
value.literal: Wang Yan sent general Ma Gui to cut the south bridge on the Yellow River; the Jin came to attack and Gui defeated them.

value.zh: 壬戌，詔軍士戰死者祿其家一年，傷重而死于營者半之。
value.en: On renxu, families of soldiers killed in battle received one year's salary; half for those who died in camp of severe wounds.
value.literal: Day renxu: an edict granted one year's salary to families of soldiers killed in battle; half for those who died in camp of severe wounds.

value.zh: 乙丑，王宣及右軍副將汲靖敗金人于蔡州確山縣。
value.en: On yichou, Wang Xuan and right-army deputy Ji Jing beat the Jin at Queshan in Cai.
value.literal: Day yichou: Wang Xuan and right-army deputy Ji Jing defeated the Jin at Queshan county in Cai prefecture.

value.zh: 趙撙棄蔡州。
value.en: Zhao Zong abandoned Cai prefecture.
value.literal: Zhao Zong abandoned Cai prefecture.

value.zh: 丙寅，金人復取之。
value.en: On bingyin, the Jin retook it.
value.literal: Day bingyin: the Jin took it again.

value.zh: 姚仲遣副將趙銓攻下鎮戎軍，金同知渭州秦弼及其子嵩來歸。
value.en: Yao Zhong's deputy Zhao Quan took Zhenrong army; Jin acting Wei commissioner Qin Bi and his son Song defected.
value.literal: Yao Zhong sent deputy Zhao Quan to take Zhenrong army; Jin acting Wei prefecture commissioner Qin Bi and his son Song came over.

value.zh: 王彥遣兵救陝州，遇金人於虢州東，敗之，金兵引去。
value.en: Wang Yan sent relief to Shan, met the Jin east of Guo, defeated them, and the Jin withdrew.
value.literal: Wang Yan sent troops to relieve Shan prefecture, met the Jin east of Guo prefecture, defeated them, and the Jin withdrew.

value.zh: 丁卯，吳珙遣將復永安軍、永寧、福昌、長水三縣。
value.en: On dingmao, Wu Gong's generals retook Yong'an army and Yongning, Fuchang, and Changshui counties.
value.literal: Day dingmao: Wu Gong sent generals to recover Yong'an army and the three counties Yongning, Fuchang, and Changshui.

value.zh: 神宗欽聖獻肅向皇后、欽成朱皇后、欽慈陳皇后、林賢妃、武賢妃 哲宗昭慈孟皇后、昭懷劉皇后 徽宗顯恭王皇后、鄭皇后、王貴妃、韋賢妃、喬貴妃、劉貴妃 欽宗朱皇后 高宗憲節邢皇后、憲聖慈烈吳皇后、潘賢妃、張賢妃、劉貴妃、劉婉儀、張貴妃 孝宗成穆郭皇后、成恭夏皇后、成肅謝皇后、蔡貴妃、李賢妃 光宗慈懿李皇后、黃貴妃 甯宗恭淑韓皇后、恭聖仁烈楊皇后 理宗謝皇后 度宗全皇后、楊淑妃
value.en: The empresses and consorts treated in this volume are: for Shenzong, Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang, Empress Qincheng Zhu, Empress Qinci Chen, and the Worthy Consorts Lin and Wu; for Zhezong, Empress Zhaoci Meng and Empress Zhaohuai Liu; for Huizong, Empress Xiangong Wang, Empress Zheng, Imperial Noble Consort Wang, and the Worthy Consorts Wei and Qiao, together with Imperial Consort Liu; for Qinzong, Empress Zhu; for Gaozong, Empress Xianjie Xing, Empress Xiansheng Cilie Wu, the Worthy Consorts Pan and Zhang, Imperial Consort Liu, Honored Lady Liu, and Imperial Noble Consort Zhang; for Xiaozong, Empresses Chengmu Guo, Chenggong Xia, and Chengsu Xie, Imperial Consort Cai, and Worthy Consort Li; for Guangzong, Empress Ciyi Li and Imperial Consort Huang; for Ningzong, Empress Gongshu Han and Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang; for Lizong, Empress Xie; and for Duzong, Empress Quan and Imperial Concubine Yang Shu.
value.literal: Under Emperor Shenzong: Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang, Empress Qincheng Zhu, Empress Qinci Chen, Worthy Consort Lin, Worthy Consort Wu. Under Emperor Zhezong: Empress Zhaoci Meng, Empress Zhaohuai Liu. Under Emperor Huizong: Empress Xiangong Wang, Empress Zheng, Imperial Noble Consort Wang, Worthy Consort Wei, Worthy Consort Qiao, Imperial Consort Liu. Under Emperor Qinzong: Empress Zhu. Under Emperor Gaozong: Empress Xianjie Xing, Empress Xiansheng Cilie Wu, Worthy Consort Pan, Worthy Consort Zhang, Imperial Consort Liu, Honored Lady Liu, Imperial Noble Consort Zhang. Under Emperor Xiaozong: Empress Chengmu Guo, Empress Chenggong Xia, Empress Chengsu Xie, Imperial Consort Cai, Worthy Consort Li. Under Emperor Guangzong: Empress Ciyi Li, Imperial Consort Huang. Under Emperor Ningzong: Empress Gongshu Han, Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang. Under Emperor Lizong: Empress Xie. Under Emperor Duzong: Empress Quan, Imperial Concubine Yang Shu.

value.zh: 六月朔，日食既，太后削「聖福」以應天變。
value.en: On the first day of the sixth month, when a solar eclipse reached totality, the empress dowager dropped "Shengfu" from her title to answer the heavenly warning.
value.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, at the completion of a solar eclipse, the empress dowager removed "Shengfu" from her title to respond to the heavenly omen.

value.zh: 丞相王爚老病，陳宜中、留夢炎庸懦無所長，日坐朝堂相爭戾。
value.en: Chief Councilor Wang Yan was old and ill. Chen Yizhong and Liu Mengyan were mediocre and timid men of no special talent, and day after day they quarreled in court.
value.literal: Chief Councilor Wang Yan was old and ill; Chen Yizhong and Liu Mengyan were mediocre, timid, and without special ability; day after day they sat in court quarreling bitterly.

value.zh: 而張世傑兵敗于焦山，宜中棄官去。
value.en: Zhang Shijie's army was defeated at Jiaoshan, and Yizhong abandoned his post and fled.
value.literal: Meanwhile Zhang Shijie's army was defeated at Jiaoshan and Yizhong abandoned his office and fled.

value.zh: 太后累召不至，遺書宜中母，使勉之。
value.en: The empress dowager summoned him repeatedly, but he would not return. She sent a letter to Yizhong's mother urging her to persuade him.
value.literal: The empress dowager repeatedly summoned him but he did not come; she sent a letter to Yizhong's mother to urge him on.

value.zh: 十月，始還朝。
value.en: In the tenth month he finally returned to court.
value.literal: In the tenth month he at last returned to court.

value.zh: 太后又親為書召夏貴等兵，曰：「吾母子不足念，獨不報先帝德乎？」
value.en: The empress dowager personally wrote again to summon the forces under Xia Gui and others, saying, "My son and I are not worth your concern—but will you not repay the kindness of the late emperor?"
value.literal: The empress dowager again personally wrote to summon the troops of Xia Gui and others, saying: "My son and I are not worth considering—but will you not repay the late emperor's kindness?"

value.zh: 貴等亦罕有至者。
value.en: Few of Xia Gui's troops came either.
value.literal: Few of Xia Gui's men came either.

value.zh: 王景，萊州掖人，家世力田。
value.en: Wang Jing came from Ye in Laizhou. His family had farmed the land for generations.
value.literal: Wang Jing was a native of Ye in Laizhou; his family for generations tilled the fields.

value.zh: 景少倜儻，善騎射，不事生業，結里中惡少為群盜。
value.en: In youth he was daring and free-spirited, an excellent horseman and archer who shunned honest work and banded with neighborhood troublemakers as outlaws.
value.literal: When young, Jing was bold and unconventional, skilled at mounted archery, did not pursue a livelihood, and joined local ruffians as a band of robbers.

value.zh: 梁大將王檀鎮滑臺，以景隸麾下，與後唐莊宗戰河上，檀有功，景嘗左右之。
value.en: Liang general Wang Tan held Huatai and took Jing into his service. In the river battles against Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong, Tan earned distinction, and Jing was often at his side.
value.literal: The Liang general Wang Tan garrisoned Huatai and placed Jing under his command; when fighting Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong on the Yellow River, Tan won merit and Jing often assisted at his side.

value.zh: 莊宗入汴，景來降，累遷奉聖都虞候。
value.en: After Zhuangzong took Bian, Jing submitted and rose through successive posts to commandant of the Fengsheng Guard.
value.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Jing came to surrender and was repeatedly promoted to commandant of the Fengsheng Guard.

value.zh: 清泰末，從張敬達圍晉陽，會契丹來援，景以所部歸晉祖。
value.en: Late in the Qingtai reign he joined Zhang Jingda's siege of Jinyang. When Khitan forces marched to relieve the city, Jing defected with his troops to the future Jin emperor.
value.literal: At the end of the Qingtai era he followed Zhang Jingda in besieging Jinyang; when the Khitan came to relieve the city, Jing brought his command over to the Jin founding emperor.

value.zh: 會契丹入中原，與趙暉、王晏謀斬契丹將劉愿，送款於漢祖。
value.en: When the Khitan overran the central plains, he joined Zhao Hui and Wang Yan in killing the Khitan general Liu Yuan and submitting to the Han emperor.
value.literal: When the Khitan entered the central plains, together with Zhao Hui and Wang Yan he plotted to behead the Khitan general Liu Yuan and sent allegiance to the Han founding emperor.

value.zh: 漢祖入汴，擢為鎮國軍節度。
value.en: When the Han emperor entered Bian, Zhang was made military governor of Zhenguo.
value.literal: When the Han founding emperor entered Bian, Zhang was promoted to military governor of Zhenguo.

value.zh: 乾祐初，加同平章事，尋移鎮邠州。
value.en: Early in Ganyou he was made co-equal chief councilor and soon transferred to Binzhou.
value.literal: At the beginning of Ganyou he was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor; soon he was transferred to garrison Binzhou.

value.zh: 章居鎮無善政，傲上剝下，以貪猥聞，用見戶為逃，擅其租賦，乃矯奏貧民數千戶負稅租，久禁繫不能輸，願以己俸代。
value.en: In his command Zhang governed badly—arrogant to superiors, harsh on subordinates, notorious for greed. He treated taxpayers as fugitives, seized their dues, then falsely reported that thousands of poor households owed back taxes, had been imprisoned unable to pay, and offered to cover the debt from his own salary.
value.literal: While holding his command Zhang had no good administration; he was arrogant toward superiors and exploited subordinates, and was known for greed and baseness. He treated registered households as fugitives and seized their rents and taxes, then falsely memorialized that several thousand poor households owed tax and rent, had long been imprisoned unable to pay, and asked to substitute his own salary.

value.zh: 時方姑息，詔褒之。
value.en: The court was in an indulgent mood and issued an edict praising him.
value.literal: The times were ones of indulgence and forbearance; an edict praised him.

value.zh: 副使趙彥鐸有良馬，章欲之不與，誣彥鐸謀逆之，殺之，亦置而不問。
value.en: Deputy Zhao Yanduo owned a fine horse. Zhang demanded it, was refused, falsely accused Zhao of treason, and killed him—with no consequences.
value.literal: Deputy commissioner Zhao Yanduo had a fine horse; Zhang wanted it but Yanduo would not give it. Zhang falsely accused Yanduo of plotting rebellion and killed him; this too was set aside without inquiry.

value.zh: 俄加檢校太師。
value.en: Soon he was made Inspector Grand Preceptor.
value.literal: Soon he was given the additional title of Inspector Grand Preceptor.

value.zh: 論曰：王景輩微時，或至為盜、負薪，遭五代之亂，奮身戎功，重據邊要。
value.en: The commentators observe: Men like Wang Jing, in their youth, were sometimes bandits or woodcutters. In the chaos of the Five Dynasties they threw themselves into military service and came to hold weighty frontier commands.
value.literal: The commentary says: Men like Wang Jing, in humble times, sometimes became bandits or carried firewood; encountering the chaos of the Five Dynasties, they threw themselves into military merit and heavily held frontier posts of importance.

value.zh: 宋興，稽顙北嚮，太祖待以誠信，宜無不自安者。
value.en: When the Song rose, they kowtowed to the north and Taizu treated them with sincerity. They should have had nothing to fear.
value.literal: When Song arose, they bowed their foreheads and turned north; Taizu treated them with sincerity and trust, and they ought all to have felt secure.

value.zh: 景趨利改圖，乃至滅族。
value.en: Yet Jing, chasing profit, changed course—and brought his clan to ruin.
value.literal: Jing, pursuing profit, changed his course, even to the extermination of his clan.

value.zh: 王晏、郭從義遷怒肆忿，誣人以死。
value.en: Wang Yan and Guo Congyi vented their rage on others and framed innocent men to death.
value.literal: Wang Yan and Guo Congyi shifted anger and vented wrath, framing men to death.

value.zh: 侯章在藩邸有剝下之名，李洪義狃於肺腑之戚，而無外凜之志，咎孰甚焉！
value.en: Hou Zhang was known for exploiting his subjects. Li Hongyi rested on family ties and lacked the outward sternness a commander needs—who was more to blame?
value.literal: Hou Zhang had a reputation at his regional command for stripping subordinates; Li Hongyi was accustomed to kinship of flesh and blood yet lacked outward awe-inspiring resolve—whose fault was the greater!

value.zh: 斯皆亂世之習，有不能盡去之者。
value.en: All of this was the habit of a chaotic age—habits not easily shed.
value.literal: These were all habits of a chaotic age; there were some that could not be entirely cast off.

value.zh: 武行德守洛邑，辯究欺罔，民用畏服，顧不優於諸人耶？
value.en: Wu Xingde held Luoyang, exposed fraud, and made the people fear and obey—was he not the better of them all?
value.literal: Wu Xingde held Luoyang, investigated and exposed deception, and the people in consequence feared and submitted—was he not rather superior to the others?

value.zh: 魯宗道
value.en: Lu Zongdao
value.literal: Lu Zongdao

value.zh: 薛奎，字宿藝，絳州正平人。
value.en: Xue Kui, whose courtesy name was Suyi, came from Zhengping in Jiangzhou.
value.literal: Xue Kui, styled Suyi, was a native of Zhengping in Jiangzhou.

value.zh: 父化光，善數術，嘗以平晉策幹太宗行在，召見不用，罷歸。
value.en: His father Huaguang was skilled in numerology and once offered Taizong a plan for pacifying Jin at the emperor's field headquarters; summoned but not employed, he went home.
value.literal: His father Huaguang was skilled in numerology and once presented a strategy for pacifying Jin at the emperor's traveling camp of Emperor Taizong; summoned and not employed, he returned home.

value.zh: 適奎始生，撫其首曰：“是子必至公輔。”
value.en: Just as Kui was born, he stroked the infant's head and said: "This child will surely rise to chief minister."
value.literal: Just as Kui was born, he stroked the child's head and said: "This boy will surely reach the rank of chief minister."

value.zh: 奎舉進士，為州第一，乃推與裏人王嚴，而處嚴下。
value.en: Kui took the jinshi examination and ranked first in the prefecture, yet yielded first place to his fellow townsman Wang Yan and placed himself below him.
value.literal: Kui passed the jinshi examination and ranked first in the prefecture, yet yielded the place to his fellow townsman Wang Yan and placed himself below Yan.

value.zh: 進士及第，為隰州軍事推官。
value.en: After passing the jinshi examination, he became military judicial officer of Xizhou.
value.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he became military judicial officer of Xizhou.

value.zh: 州民常聚博僧舍，一日，盜殺寺奴取財去，博者適至，血偶涴衣，邏卒捕送州，考訊誣伏。
value.en: The people of the prefecture often gambled in a Buddhist monastery. One day a thief killed a temple servant and made off with the goods. Gamblers arrived just then, and blood happened to stain their clothes. Patrolmen seized them and sent them to the prefecture, where interrogation forced false confessions.
value.literal: The people of the prefecture often gathered to gamble in a Buddhist monastery. One day a thief killed a temple slave and took the goods away; gamblers happened to arrive, and blood happened to stain their clothes. Patrol soldiers seized and sent them to the prefecture; under interrogation they falsely confessed.

value.zh: 奎獨疑之，白州緩其獄，後果得殺人者。
value.en: Kui alone doubted the case, persuaded the prefect to delay judgment, and later found the real killer.
value.literal: Kui alone doubted the case, reported to the prefecture to slow the trial, and later indeed obtained the real murderer.

value.zh: 徙儀州推官，嘗部丁夫運糧至鹽州，會久雨，粟麥漬腐，奎白轉運盧之翰，請縱民還州而償所失。
value.en: Transferred to judicial officer of Yizhou, he once led corvée laborers hauling grain to Yanzhou. After long rains the grain and wheat rotted. Kui reported to transport commissioner Lu Zhihan and asked to send the laborers home while making good the loss.
value.literal: Transferred to judicial officer of Yizhou, he once led corvée laborers transporting grain to Yanzhou. Prolonged rain caused the grain and wheat to soak and rot. Kui reported to the transport commissioner Lu Zhihan, requesting to release the people back to the prefecture while compensating the loss.

value.zh: 之翰怒，欲劾奏之。
value.en: Zhihan was angry and wanted to impeach him.
value.literal: Zhihan was angry and wished to memorialize and impeach him.

value.zh: 奎徐曰：“用兵久，人疲轉餉，今幸兵食有餘，安用此陳腐以困民哉！”
value.en: Kui said calmly: "The army has been at war for years and the people are exhausted hauling supplies. We are fortunate that military stores are ample—why trouble them with rotten grain?"
value.literal: Kui said calmly: "The army has been employed a long time and the people are weary of transporting provisions. Now fortunately military food is abundant—why use this stale grain to trouble the people!"

value.zh: 之翰意解，凡民所失，悉奏除之。
value.en: Zhihan relented, and all losses borne by the people were memorialized for remission.
value.literal: Zhihan's mind was eased, and all the people's losses were memorialized for remission.

value.zh: 改大理寺丞、知莆田縣。
value.en: He was made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Putian County.
value.literal: He was changed to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Putian County.

value.zh: 請蠲南閩時稅鹹魚、蒲草錢。
value.en: He petitioned to abolish the wartime taxes on salted fish and sedge grass in southern Fujian.
value.literal: He requested remission of the wartime taxes on salted fish and sedge in southern Min.

value.zh: 种世衡
value.en: Zhong Shiheng
value.literal: Zhong Shiheng

value.zh: 初，世衡在青澗城，元昊未臣，其貴人野利剛浪㖫、遇乞兄弟有材謀，皆號大王。
value.en: Earlier, while Shiheng held Qingjian, Yuan Hao had not yet submitted to the Song. Yuan's chief advisers, the brothers Yeli Ganglangrang and Yuji, were men of talent and strategy, and each was called a Great King.
value.literal: Earlier, when Shiheng was at Qingjian Fort, Yuan Hao had not yet submitted; his nobles Yeli Ganglangrang and the brothers Yuji were talented in strategy and all were styled Great Kings.

value.zh: 親信用事，邊臣欲以謀間之。
value.en: They were Yuan's trusted inner circle, and the border officials hoped to drive a wedge between them.
value.literal: They were trusted intimates in power, and border officials wished to estrange them by stratagem.

value.zh: 慶曆二年，鄜延經略使龐籍，兩為保安軍守劉拯書，賂蕃部破醜以達野利兄弟，而涇原路王沿、葛懷敏亦遣人持書及金寶以遣遇乞。
value.en: In Qingli year 2, Pang Ji, commissioner of the Fuyan frontier, twice had Liu Zheng, defender of Bao'an Army, write letters and bribe the tribesman Pochou to reach the Yeli brothers. Wang Yan and Ge Huaimin of Jingyuan circuit also sent envoys with letters and gold and jewels to Yuji.
value.literal: In the second year of Qingli, Fuyan Frontier Commissioner Pang Ji twice had Bao'an Army defender Liu Zheng write, bribing the tribal people Pochou to reach the Yeli brothers, while Jingyuan Circuit's Wang Yan and Ge Huaimin also sent men bearing letters and gold and jewels to present to Yuji.

value.zh: 會剛浪㖫令浪埋、賞乞、媚娘等三人詣世衡請降，世衡知其詐，曰：「與其殺之，不若因以為間。」
value.en: Just then Ganglangrang sent three men—Langmai, Shangqi, and Meiniang—to Shiheng offering surrender. Shiheng saw through the ruse and said, "Better to turn them into a wedge than to kill them."
value.literal: It happened that Ganglangrang sent Langmai, Shangqi, Meiniang, and three others to Shiheng to request surrender; Shiheng knew it was deceit and said, "Rather than kill them, better use them for estrangement."

value.zh: 留使監商稅，出入騎從甚寵。
value.en: He kept them to supervise trade taxes and treated them with conspicuous honor whenever they went abroad.
value.literal: He retained them to supervise commercial taxes, and in going out and in they were greatly favored in mounted escort.

value.zh: 有僧王光信者，趫勇善騎射，習知蕃部山川道路。
value.en: A monk named Wang Guangxin was swift, brave, and expert with bow and horse, and knew every trail in the tribal country.
value.literal: There was a monk Wang Guangxin, nimble and brave, skilled in mounted archery, thoroughly knowing the mountains, rivers, and roads of the tribal lands.

value.zh: 世衡出兵，常使為鄉導，數蕩族帳，奏以為三班借職，改名嵩。
value.en: Shiheng often used him as guide on campaign and sent him repeatedly against tribal camps. He memorialized for him a third-class attendant post on probation and gave him the name Song.
value.literal: When Shiheng sent troops he often used him as guide, repeatedly raiding tribal camps; he memorialized appointing him Acting Third Class Attendant and changed his name to Song.

value.zh: 世衡為蠟書，遣嵩遺剛浪㖫，言浪埋等已至，朝廷知王有向漢心，命為夏州節度使，奉錢月萬緡，旌節已至，趣其歸附，以棗綴畫龜，喻其早歸之意。
value.en: Shiheng wrote a secret letter in wax, sent Song to deliver it to Ganglangrang, and claimed that Langmai and the others had already arrived, that the court knew the king favored the Song, that he had been appointed military commissioner of Xia with ten thousand strings of cash each month, and that the imperial commission was already on its way. He urged quick submission and sketched a tortoise with jujube stems to suggest "return soon."
value.literal: Shiheng made a wax-sealed letter and sent Song to present it to Ganglangrang, saying Langmai and the others had already arrived, the court knew the king had a heart inclined toward Han, appointed him Military Commissioner of Xia Prefecture with ten thousand strings monthly, insignia of office had arrived, urging his submission, and with jujube strings drew a tortoise to suggest the meaning of early return.

value.zh: 剛浪㖫得書大懼，自所治執嵩歸元昊。
value.en: Ganglangrang was terrified, seized Song in his own territory, and handed him over to Yuan Hao.
value.literal: Ganglangrang received the letter and was greatly afraid; from his own domain he seized Song and returned him to Yuan Hao.

value.zh: 元昊疑剛浪㖫貳己，不得還所治，且錮嵩穽中。
value.en: Yuan Hao suspected Ganglangrang of treachery, refused to let him return to his domain, and threw Song into a dungeon.
value.literal: Yuan Hao suspected Ganglangrang of disloyalty to himself, would not let him return to his domain, and moreover imprisoned Song in a pit.

value.zh: 使其臣李文貴以剛浪㖫旨報世衡，且言不達所遺書意，或許通和，願賜一言。
value.en: He sent his minister Li Wengui to Shiheng in Ganglangrang's name, saying he had not understood the letter and that peace might be possible if the Song would send a reply.
value.literal: He sent his minister Li Wengui to report to Shiheng in Ganglangrang's name, and added he did not grasp the meaning of the letter sent, perhaps peace might be allowed, and begged a word be granted.

value.zh: 世衡以白籍。
value.en: Shiheng reported this to Pang Ji.
value.literal: Shiheng reported this to Pang Ji.

value.zh: 時朝廷已欲招拊，籍召文貴至，諭以國家寬大開納意，縱使還報。
value.en: The court was already seeking reconciliation. Pang Ji summoned Wengui, explained the empire's willingness to receive them generously, and sent him back with a reply.
value.literal: The court already wished to win them over; Ji summoned Wengui, instructed him in the state's broad and open acceptance, and released him to return with report.

value.zh: 元昊得報，出嵩，禮之甚厚，使與文貴偕來。
value.en: Yuan Hao received the answer, freed Song, treated him with great honor, and sent him back with Wengui.
value.literal: Yuan Hao received the reply, released Song, treated him with great honor, and had him come together with Wengui.

value.zh: 自是繼遣使者請降，遂稱臣如舊。
value.en: Envoys requesting peace followed in succession, and Yuan Hao submitted as a vassal as he had once done.
value.literal: From this he successively sent envoys requesting surrender and at last submitted as vassal as before.

value.zh: 世衡聞野利兄弟已誅，為文越境祭之。
value.en: When Shiheng learned that the Yeli brothers had been executed, he wrote a memorial text and crossed the border to offer sacrifice for them.
value.literal: Shiheng heard the Yeli brothers had been executed and composed a text to cross the border and sacrifice to them.

value.zh: 籍疏嵩勞，具言元昊未通時，世衡畫策遣嵩冒艱險間其君臣，遂成猜貳，因此與中國通，請優進嵩官。
value.en: Pang Ji memorialized to reward Song, explaining that before Yuan Hao submitted, Shiheng had plotted to send Song through great danger to sow distrust between ruler and ministers, which had opened the way to peace with the Song, and asked that Song be promoted.
value.literal: Ji memorialized to reward Song, fully stating that before Yuan Hao had submitted, Shiheng had devised the plan and sent Song through hardship and peril to estrange ruler and ministers, thereby achieving suspicion and division, and through this communication with China was opened; he requested preferential advancement of Song's office.

value.zh: 遷三班奉職。
value.en: Song was promoted to third-class service attendant.
value.literal: He was transferred to Third Class Service Attendant.

value.zh: 後嵩因對自陳，又進侍禁、閤門祗候。
value.en: Later, when Song appeared at court in person, he was advanced again to palace guard attendant and gatehouse attendant.
value.literal: Later Song on audience stated his own case and was further advanced to Palace Attendant Guard and Gatehouse Attendant.

value.zh: 白時中 徐處仁 馮澥 王倫 宇文虛中 湯思退
value.en: Bai Shizhong, Xu Churen, Feng Xie, Wang Lun, Yu Wenxuzhong, and Tang Situi
value.literal: Bai Shizhong, Xu Churen, Feng Xie, Wang Lun, Yu Wenxuzhong, Tang Situi

value.zh: 既而金專事殺戮，上意中悔，思退復密令孫造諭敵以重兵脅和。
value.en: When the Jin turned to slaughter the emperor regretted it; Situi secretly had Sun Zao tell them to coerce peace with heavy troops.
value.literal: Before long the Jin devoted themselves to slaughter; the emperor's heart midway regretted; Situi again secretly had Sun Zao tell the enemy to coerce peace with heavy troops.

value.zh: 上聞有敵兵，命建康都統王彥等禦之，仍命思退督江、淮軍，辭不行。
value.en: Hearing of enemy troops, the emperor ordered Wang Yan to resist and Situi to supervise Jiang and Huai armies; he declined.
value.literal: When the emperor heard of enemy troops he ordered Jiankang Commander Wang Yan and others to resist, and also ordered Situi to supervise Jiang and Huai armies; he declined and would not go.

value.zh: 僕散忠義自清河口渡淮，言者極論思退急和撤備之罪，遂罷相，尋責居永州。
value.en: Pusan Zhongyi crossed the Huai at Qinghekou; critics attacked Situi for rushing peace and withdrawing defenses; he was dismissed and banished to Yongzhou.
value.literal: Pusan Zhongyi crossed the Huai at Qinghekou; remonstrators fiercely criticized Situi for urgently seeking peace and withdrawing defenses; he was dismissed as chancellor and soon banished to Yongzhou.

value.zh: 於是太學生張觀等七十二人上書，論思退、王之望、尹穡等奸邪誤國，招致敵人，請斬之。
value.en: Seventy-two Imperial Academy students led by Zhang Guan memorialized that Situi, Wang Zhiwang, and Yin Ji had misled the state and invited the enemy, begging their execution.
value.literal: Thereupon seventy-two students of the Imperial Academy led by Zhang Guan memorialized that Situi, Wang Zhiwang, Yin Ji, and others were wicked and misled the state, inviting the enemy, and begged their execution.

value.zh: 思退憂悸死。
value.en: Situi died of fear and agitation.
value.literal: Situi died of fear and agitation.

value.zh: 樓鑰，字大防，明州鄞縣人。
value.en: Lou Yao, courtesy name Dafang, came from Yin County in Mingzhou.
value.literal: Lou Yao, styled Dafang, was a native of Yin County in Ming Prefecture.

value.zh: 隆興元年，試南宮，有司偉其辭藝，欲以冠多士，策偶犯舊諱，知貢舉洪遵奏，得旨以冠末等。
value.en: In Longxing 1 (1163), he sat for the metropolitan examination. The examiners admired his writing and intended to rank him first, but his policy essay inadvertently violated an old naming taboo. Chief examiner Hong Zun reported this, and by imperial order Lou was placed last among the highest tier of graduates.
value.literal: In the first year of Longxing, he tested at the Southern Palace examination; the officials admired his literary skill and wished to place him first among the successful candidates, but his policy essay accidentally violated an old taboo name; Hong Zun, the chief examiner, memorialized, and he received the imperial decision to be ranked last among the top tier.

value.zh: 投贄謝諸公，考官胡銓稱之曰：「此翰林才也。」
value.en: When he submitted a letter of thanks to the examiners, Hu Quan, one of the examiners, praised him: "This man has the makings of a Hanlin academician."
value.literal: Presenting a letter of thanks to the examiners, the examiner Hu Quan praised him, saying: "This is talent fit for the Hanlin Academy."

value.zh: 試教官，調溫州教授，為敕令所刪定官，修《淳熙法》。
value.en: He passed the instructor examination, was appointed professor at Wenzhou, served as a reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office, and helped compile the Chunxi Code.
value.literal: He passed the instructor examination, was assigned as professor at Wenzhou, served as a reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office, and compiled the Chunxi Code.

value.zh: 議者欲降太學釋奠為中祀，鑰曰：「乘輿臨幸，於先聖則拜，武成則肅揖，其禮異矣，可鈞敵乎？」
value.en: Debaters proposed lowering the Imperial Academy's Confucian sacrifice from a major to a medium-grade rite. Lou objected: "When the emperor visits in person, he bows to Confucius but only performs a formal clasped-hand salute at the Wu Cheng shrine — the ceremonies are already unequal. How can they be treated as equivalent?"
value.literal: Some in debate wished to downgrade the Imperial Academy's sacrifice to Confucius to a medium-grade rite; Yao said: "When the imperial carriage visits in person, one bows to the Former Sage but performs a solemn bow with hands clasped to Wu Cheng — the rites already differ; can they be made equal?"

value.zh: 王炎宣撫川、陝，辟為幹辦公事。
value.en: Wang Yan was dispatched to pacify Sichuan and Shaanxi and recruited him as administrative officer.
value.literal: Wang Yan was dispatched to pacify Chuan and Shan and recruited him as administrative officer.

value.zh: 游為炎陳進取之策，以為經略中原必自長安始，取長安必自隴右始。
value.en: You presented Yan a strategy of advance: to recover the Central Plain one must begin at Chang'an, and to take Chang'an one must begin at Longyou.
value.literal: You presented Yan a strategy of advance, holding that to plan the Central Plain one must begin at Chang'an, and to take Chang'an one must begin at Longyou.

value.zh: 當積粟練兵，有釁則攻，無則守。
value.en: Accumulate grain and drill troops — attack when opportunity opens, defend when it does not.
value.literal: One should accumulate grain and drill troops — attack when there is an opening, defend when there is none.

value.zh: 吳璘子挺代掌兵，頗驕恣，傾財結士，屢以過誤殺人，炎莫誰何。
value.en: Wu Lin's son Ting took command, arrogant and willful, spending wealth to win scholars and repeatedly killing men through negligence — Yan could not restrain him.
value.literal: Wu Lin's son Ting took command of the army, quite arrogant and willful, spending wealth to win over scholars, repeatedly killing men through errors — Yan could do nothing.

value.zh: 游請以玠子拱代挺。
value.en: You asked that Wu Jie's son Gong replace Ting.
value.literal: You asked that Jie's son Gong replace Ting.

value.zh: 炎曰：「拱怯而寡謀，遇敵必敗。」
value.en: Yan said: "Gong is timid and lacks strategy; he will surely be defeated."
value.literal: Yan said: "Gong is timid and lacks strategy; meeting the enemy he will surely be defeated."

value.zh: 游曰：「使挺遇敵，安保其不敗。
value.en: You replied: "If Ting meets the enemy, who guarantees he will not be defeated?
value.literal: You said: "If Ting meets the enemy, who guarantees he will not be defeated?

value.zh: 就令有功，愈不可駕馭。」
value.en: Even if he won battles, he would be harder still to control."
value.literal: Even if he had merit, he would be all the harder to control."

value.zh: 及挺子曦僭叛，游言始驗。
value.en: When Ting's son Xi rebelled, You's warning was vindicated.
value.literal: When Ting's son Xi rebelled in usurpation, You's words were verified.

value.zh: 儒林四
value.en: Confucian Scholars 4
value.literal: Confucian Scholars 4.

value.zh: 樞密使王炎薦於朝，召為大理寺主簿，未至，為書謝炎曰：“主上天資英特，群臣無將順緝熙之具，幸得遭時，不能格心正始，以建中興之業，徒僥幸功利，誇言以眩俗，雖復中夏，猶無益也。
value.en: Wang Yan of the Privy Council recommended him to court; he was called up as chief clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, but before he arrived he wrote Yan a letter of refusal: "The Son of Heaven is gifted beyond the ordinary, yet his ministers have no way to guide and steady him; given the moment, they cannot set his heart straight at the start and build a true restoration—they chase quick results and bedazzle the world with empty boasts; even retaking the north would change little.
value.literal: Privy Councilor Wang Yan recommended him to the court; he was summoned as chief clerk of the Court of Judicial Review but had not yet arrived when he wrote Yan to decline, saying: "Our ruler is talented and exceptional, yet the ministers lack the means to harmonize and brighten him; though fortune has placed him in office, they cannot rectify the heart and set a true beginning to build the enterprise of restoration—they merely grasp at expedient gain and dazzle the age with boastful words; even if the Central Plains were recovered, it would still be of no benefit.

value.zh: 為今之計，莫若以仁義紀綱為本。
value.en: The right course now is to take benevolence, righteousness, and the fundamental norms as the foundation.
value.literal: For the policy of the present, nothing surpasses taking benevolence and righteousness and the great norms as the root.

value.zh: 至於用兵，請俟十年之後可也。”
value.en: As for going to war, that should wait ten years."
value.literal: As for using troops, please wait until ten years have passed.

value.zh: 孝武帝二十八男：文穆皇后生廢帝子業、豫章王子尚，陳淑媛生晉安王子勛，阮容華生安陸王子綏，徐昭容生皇子子深，何淑儀生松滋侯子房，史昭華生臨海王子頊，殷貴妃生始平孝敬王子鸞，次永嘉王子仁，與皇子子深同生，何婕妤生皇子子鳳，謝昭容生始安王子真，江婕妤生皇子子玄，史昭儀生邵陵王子元，次齊敬王子羽，與始平孝敬王子鸞同生，江美人生皇子子衡，楊婕妤生淮南王子孟，次皇子子況，與皇子子玄同生，次南平王子產，與永嘉王子仁同生，次晉陵孝王子雲，次皇子子文，並與始平孝敬王子鸞同生，次廬陵王子輿，與淮南王子孟同生，次南海哀王子師，與始平孝敬王子鸞同生，次淮陽思王子霄，與皇子子玄同生，次皇子子雍，與始安王子真同生，次皇子子趨，與皇子子鳳同生，次皇子子期，與皇子子衡同生，次東平王子嗣，與始安王子真同生，杜容華生皇子子悅。
value.en: Emperor Xiaowu had twenty-eight sons. Empress Wenmu bore the Deposed Emperor Ziye and Yuzhang Prince Zi Shang. Lady Chen bore Jin'an Prince Zi Xun. Ruan Ronghua bore Anlu Prince Zi Sui. Xu Zhaorong bore Prince Zi Shen. He Shuyi bore Songzi Marquis Zi Fang. Shi Zhaohua bore Linhai Prince Zi Xu. Noble Consort Yin bore Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, then Yongjia Prince Zi Ren (twins with Prince Zi Shen). Lady He bore Prince Zi Feng. Xie Zhaorong bore Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen. Lady Jiang bore Prince Zi Xuan. Lady Shi bore Shaoling Prince Zi Yuan, then Qi Jing Prince Zi Yu (twins with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan). Lady Jiang bore Prince Zi Heng. Lady Yang bore Huainan Prince Zi Meng, then Prince Zi Kuang (twins with Prince Zi Xuan), then Nanping Prince Zi Chan (twins with Yongjia Prince Zi Ren), then Jinling Xiao Prince Zi Yun and Prince Zi Wen (all twins with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan), then Luling Prince Zi Yu (twins with Huainan Prince Zi Meng), then Nanhai Ai Prince Zi Shi (twins with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan), then Huaiyang Si Prince Zi Xiao (twins with Prince Zi Xuan), then Prince Zi Yong (twins with Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen), then Prince Zi Qu (twins with Prince Zi Feng), then Prince Zi Qi (twins with Prince Zi Heng), then Dongping Prince Zi Si (twins with Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen). Du Ronghua bore Prince Zi Yue.
value.literal: Emperor Xiaowu had twenty-eight sons: Empress Wenmu bore the Deposed Emperor Ziye and Yuzhang Prince Zi Shang; Lady Chen bore Jin'an Prince Zi Xun; Ruan Ronghua bore Anlu Prince Zi Sui; Xu Zhaorong bore Prince Zi Shen; He Shuyi bore Songzi Marquis Zi Fang; Shi Zhaohua bore Linhai Prince Zi Xu; Noble Consort Yin bore Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, next Yongjia Prince Zi Ren, born together with Prince Zi Shen; Lady He bore Prince Zi Feng; Xie Zhaorong bore Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen; Lady Jiang bore Prince Zi Xuan; Lady Shi bore Shaoling Prince Zi Yuan, next Qi Jing Prince Zi Yu, born together with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan; Lady Jiang bore Prince Zi Heng; Lady Yang bore Huainan Prince Zi Meng, next Prince Zi Kuang, born together with Prince Zi Xuan, next Nanping Prince Zi Chan, born together with Yongjia Prince Zi Ren, next Jinling Xiao Prince Zi Yun, next Prince Zi Wen, all born together with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, next Luling Prince Zi Yu, born together with Huainan Prince Zi Meng, next Nanhai Ai Prince Zi Shi, born together with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, next Huaiyang Si Prince Zi Xiao, born together with Prince Zi Xuan, next Prince Zi Yong, born together with Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen, next Prince Zi Qu, born together with Prince Zi Feng, next Prince Zi Qi, born together with Prince Zi Heng, next Dongping Prince Zi Si, born together with Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen; Du Ronghua bore Prince Zi Yue.

value.zh: 安陸王子綏、南平王子產、廬陵王子輿並出繼。
value.en: Anlu Prince Zi Sui, Nanping Prince Zi Chan, and Luling Prince Zi Yu were all given in adoption to continue other lines.
value.literal: Anlu Prince Zi Sui, Nanping Prince Zi Chan, and Luling Prince Zi Yu were all adopted out as heirs.

value.zh: 皇子子深、子鳳、子玄、子衡、子況、子文、子雍未封，早夭。
value.en: Princes Zi Shen, Zi Feng, Zi Xuan, Zi Heng, Zi Kuang, Zi Wen, and Zi Yong were never enfeoffed and died in childhood.
value.literal: Princes Zi Shen, Zi Feng, Zi Xuan, Zi Heng, Zi Kuang, Zi Wen, and Zi Yong received no fiefs and died young.

value.zh: 子趨、子期、子悅未封，為明帝所殺。
value.en: Zi Qu, Zi Qi, and Zi Yue had received no fiefs when Emperor Ming had them put to death.
value.literal: Zi Qu, Zi Qi, and Zi Yue received no fiefs and were killed by Emperor Ming.

value.zh: 太宗即位，改督為都督，進號安東將軍，太守如故。
value.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Zi Fang's supervisory command was elevated to full commandership, he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East, and he retained his post as governor.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, his command was changed from supervisor to commander-in-chief, he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East, and his governorship was unchanged.

value.zh: 又徵為撫軍，領太常。
value.en: He was also recalled to serve as General Who Pacifies the Army and concurrently as Minister of Rites.
value.literal: He was also summoned as General Who Pacifies the Army and concurrently headed the Ministry of Rites.

value.zh: 長史孔覬不受命，舉兵反，應晉安王。
value.en: Chief Administrator Kong Xian refused to obey, raised troops in revolt, and rallied to Jin'an Prince.
value.literal: Chief Administrator Kong Xian refused the order, raised troops in rebellion, and responded to Jin'an Prince.

value.zh: 子勛即偽位，進子房號車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。
value.en: When Zi Xun took the rebel throne, he promoted Zi Fang to General of Chariots and Cavalry with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.
value.literal: When Zi Xun took the false throne, he advanced Zi Fang's title to General of Chariots and Cavalry with an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies.

value.zh: 三吳晉陵並受命於覬。
value.en: The Three Wu commanderies and Jinling all submitted to Kong Xian's authority.
value.literal: The Three Wu regions and Jinling all accepted orders from Xian.

value.zh: 太宗遣衞將軍巴陵王休若督諸將吳喜等東討，戰無不捷，以次平定。
value.en: Emperor Ming sent Guards General Prince of Baling Xiu Ruo to lead generals including Wu Xi in an eastern campaign. They won every battle and pacified the region step by step.
value.literal: Emperor Ming sent Guards General Prince of Baling Xiu Ruo to command the generals Wu Xi and others in an eastern campaign; in battle they were never unsuccessful, and the regions were pacified in succession.

value.zh: 上虞令王晏起兵殺覬，囚子房，送還京都，上宥之，貶為松滋縣侯，食邑千戶。
value.en: Shangyu Magistrate Wang Yan raised troops, killed Kong Xian, imprisoned Zi Fang, and sent him to the capital. The Emperor spared his life but demoted him to Marquis of Songzi with a fief of one thousand households.
value.literal: Magistrate of Shangyu Wang Yan raised troops, killed Xian, imprisoned Zi Fang, and sent him back to the capital; the Emperor pardoned him and demoted him to Marquis of Songzi county with a fief of one thousand households.

value.zh: 燕鳳 許謙 張袞 崔玄伯 鄧淵
value.en: Biographies of Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Zhang Gun, Cui Xuanbo, and Deng Yuan
value.literal: Yan Feng; Xu Qian; Zhang Gun; Cui Xuanbo; Deng Yuan

value.zh: 計彼主篡殺之迹，人鬼同知，疑親猜貴，早暴遐邇。
value.en: Weigh that lord's usurpation and murder — known to men and spirits alike; suspicion of kin and mistrust of the noble were long ago plain far and near.
value.literal: Consider the traces of that lord's usurpation and murder — known alike to men and spirits; suspicion of kin and mistrust of the noble long ago exposed far and near.

value.zh: 兄投心逆節，千載何名！
value.en: Elder brother, to set your heart on rebellion — what name will stand for a thousand years?
value.literal: Elder brother, to cast your heart into rebellion — what name for a thousand years!

value.zh: 物患無施，器非時用，生不振世，沒無令聲，先師以為鄙，君子以為耻。
value.en: When things have no place to be used and vessels are unfit for the age, to live without stirring the world and die without a fair name — the ancients called that base, gentlemen called it shame.
value.literal: When things have no scope for use and vessels are unfit for the time, one who lives without stirring the age and dies without a fair reputation — the former masters held this base, gentlemen held it shameful.

value.zh: 此則事困伎殫，自勉無益，故其宜矣。
value.en: Here affairs are tight and arts spent; urging oneself on brings no gain — hence the proper course.
value.literal: Here events are straitened and skills exhausted; self-exhortation brings no gain — hence the fit course.

value.zh: 以兄之才，夙超鄉土，如弟之徒，誰不瞻仰，每尋昔念，未敢忘懷。
value.en: With your talent, elder brother, you have long outshone our homeland — who like me does not look up to you? I never dare forget our old bond.
value.literal: With elder brother's talent, from old surpassing your homeland — who among men like me does not look up to you? Whenever I recall former thoughts, I dare not forget.

value.zh: 雖復途遙二千，心想若對，敬遵軌範，以資一生。
value.en: Though two thousand li lie between us, in thought we meet as face to face; reverently I follow your example for my whole life.
value.literal: Though the road spans two thousand li, in thought we meet face to face; reverently I follow the norm and draw on it for a lifetime.

value.zh: 今名可揚矣而不能顯親，事可變矣而不能離辱，故世之所未解也。
value.en: Now fame could be raised yet you cannot honor your kin; affairs could be changed yet you cannot shake off disgrace — that is what the age cannot understand.
value.literal: Now fame could be raised yet you cannot glorify kin; affairs could be changed yet you cannot leave disgrace — hence what the age has not understood.

value.zh: 且君子在家也不過孝於其親，入朝也不過忠於其君。
value.en: A gentleman at home is filial to his kin; in court he is loyal to his lord — no more.
value.literal: And the gentleman at home does no more than show filial piety to his kin; in court does no more than show loyalty to his lord.

value.zh: 主上之於兄，恩則不可酬，義則不可背。
value.en: The sovereign's treatment of you, elder brother — grace that cannot be repaid, righteousness that cannot be betrayed.
value.literal: The sovereign's treatment of elder brother — in grace it cannot be repaid, in righteousness it cannot be betrayed.

value.zh: 身可殺也，故非其酬；
value.en: One's person may be given up — that is not repayment;
value.literal: The person may be killed — hence this is not the repayment;

value.zh: 功不逮也，故非其報。
value.en: merit does not stretch so far — that is not return.
value.literal: Merit does not reach so far — hence this is not the return.

value.zh: 今可以效矣而又弗為，非孝也。
value.en: Now you could act loyally and again you will not — that is unfilial.
value.literal: Now you could effect loyalty yet again do not — this is unfilial.

value.zh: 即實而言，兄之不變，得為忠乎？
value.en: Judged by fact, elder brother, can your refusal to change count as loyalty?
value.literal: Judged by fact, elder brother's not changing — can this count as loyalty?

value.zh: 至於講武爭強，不敵者久矣；
value.en: As for drilling in arms and contending for mastery, you have long been unmatched;
value.literal: As for training in arms and contending for supremacy, the unmatched have long been so;

value.zh: 論安與危，不同者驗矣；
value.en: weigh safety against peril and the unlike cases have been proved;
value.literal: Discussing security and danger, those not alike have been proved;

value.zh: 羣情背去，獨留者謬矣。
value.en: the crowd's heart has turned away — to stand alone is error.
value.literal: Mass sentiment turns away in desertion; to remain alone is error.

value.zh: 願深察之。
value.en: I beg you to weigh this deeply.
value.literal: I beg deep scrutiny of this.

value.zh: 王晏道絕外交，器非雄朗，專華保望，便就屠割。
value.en: Wang Yan cut off every outside tie; his talent was not bold and bright; clinging to glory and nursing hope, he was at once put to the sword.
value.literal: Wang Yan utterly cut off external ties; his capacity was not heroic and bright; clinging to splendor and guarding hope, he was at once sent to slaughter.

value.zh: 方之於兄，其全百倍。
value.en: Compared with you, elder brother, he was not one part in a hundred.
value.literal: Compared with elder brother, you are whole a hundredfold.

value.zh: 且淮蕃海捍，本出北豪，壽春之任，兄何由免？
value.en: Moreover the Huai frontier and the coastal garrisons bred northern champions — could you, elder brother, escape the Shouchun command?
value.literal: Moreover the Huai lands and the coastal marches originally produced northern champions — could elder brother escape the charge at Shouchun?

value.zh: 以是而言，猜嫌已決。
value.en: On that ground suspicion is already fixed.
value.literal: On this ground, suspicion and mistrust are already settled.

value.zh: 又宗門未幾，南北莫寄，先構之重，非兄何託，受社之榮，鄙心之相望矣。
value.en: Moreover the house is still young; north and south have nowhere else to lodge — to whom but you, elder brother, can the weight of the founding be entrusted? The glory of receiving a fief — my humble heart has long looked for it.
value.literal: Moreover the ancestral house is not many generations old; north and south have no other lodging — to whom but elder brother can the weight of the prior structure be entrusted? The glory of receiving a fief — this humble heart has longed for it.

value.zh: 今執志不寤，忠孝兩忘，王晏之辜，安能自保，見機而作，其在茲乎。
value.en: Now you cling to your resolve without waking, forgetting both filial piety and loyalty — Wang Yan's guilt, how could he save himself? To act when the moment shows itself — is it not now?
value.literal: Now clinging to resolve without waking, both filial piety and loyalty forgotten — Wang Yan's crime, how can he protect himself? To act when the moment appears — is it not here?

value.zh: 王肅 宋弁
value.en: Wang Su; Song Bian
value.literal: Wang Su; Song Bian

value.zh: 肅弟秉，字文政。
value.en: Su's younger brother Bing, whose courtesy name was Wenzheng.
value.literal: Su's younger brother Bing, styled Wenzheng.

value.zh: 涉獵書史，微有兄風。
value.en: He read widely in books and histories and showed something of his elder brother's manner.
value.literal: He ranged through books and histories and had a slight trace of his elder brother's manner.

value.zh: 世宗初，攜兄子誦、翊、衍等入國，拜中書郎，遷司徒諮議，出為輔國將軍、幽州刺史。
value.en: Early in the Shizong reign he brought his elder brother's sons Song, Yi, Yan, and others into Wei territory. He was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, then Adviser to the Minister of Education, and later sent out as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of You Province.
value.literal: At the beginning of Shizong, he brought his elder brother's sons Song, Yi, Yan, and others into the state; he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, and sent out as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of You Province.

value.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、徐州刺史。
value.en: He died and was posthumously made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Xuzhou.
value.literal: He died; posthumously granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Xuzhou.

value.zh: 袁躍 裴敬憲 盧觀 封肅 邢臧 裴伯茂 邢昕 溫子昇
value.en: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, and Wen Zisheng
value.literal: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, Wen Zisheng

value.zh: 正光末，廣陽王淵為東北道行臺，召為郎中，軍國文翰皆出其手。
value.en: At the end of Zhengguang, Prince Yuan of Guangyang served as Northeast Circuit Commander and summoned Zisheng as Gentleman; all military and state papers came from his hand.
value.literal: At the end of Zhengguang, Prince Yuan of Guangyang served as Northeast Circuit Commander; he summoned Zisheng as Gentleman; all military and state documents issued from his hand.

value.zh: 於是才名轉盛。
value.en: His fame for talent then grew still greater.
value.literal: Thereupon his fame for talent grew still greater.

value.zh: 黃門郎徐紇受四方表啟，答之敏速，於淵獨沉思曰：「彼有溫郎中，才藻可畏。」
value.en: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu Hong received memorials from the four quarters and answered them swiftly; facing Yuan alone he mused and said, "They have Gentleman Wen on staff—his literary power inspires dread."
value.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu Hong received memorials from the four directions and answered swiftly; facing Yuan alone he pondered and said: "They have Gentleman Wen there—his literary talent is formidable."

value.zh: 高車破走，珍實盈滿，子昇取絹四十匹。
value.en: When the Gaoche were routed, booty filled the tents; Zisheng took forty bolts of silk.
value.literal: When the Gaoche were routed and fled, treasures filled the camp; Zisheng took forty bolts of silk.

value.zh: 及淵為葛榮所害，子昇亦見羈執。
value.en: When Yuan was slain by Ge Rong, Zisheng too was seized and detained.
value.literal: When Yuan was killed by Ge Rong, Zisheng was also seized and held.

value.zh: 榮下都督和洛興與子昇舊識，以數十騎潛送子昇，得達冀州。
value.en: Heluo Xing, a subordinate commander under Rong and an old acquaintance of Zisheng, secretly escorted him with several dozen horsemen until he reached Jizhou.
