value.literal: Ge Rong's subordinate commander Heluo Xing was an old acquaintance of Zisheng; with several dozen horsemen he secretly sent Zisheng off, enabling him to reach Jizhou.

value.zh: 還京，李楷執其手曰：「卿今得免，足使夷甫慚德。」
value.en: On returning to the capital, Li Kai grasped his hand and said, "You have come through alive—enough to make Yifu blush for his character."
value.literal: Returning to the capital, Li Kai took his hand and said: "You have now escaped—enough to make Yifu ashamed of his virtue."

value.zh: 自是無復宦情，閉門讀書，厲精不已。
value.en: From then on he lost all desire for office, shut his door to read, and honed his mind without cease.
value.literal: From then on he had no further desire for office, shut his door and read books, and refined his mind without cease.

value.zh: 房琯，字次律，河南河南人。
value.en: Fang Guan, whose courtesy name was Cilü, came from Henan in Henan commandery.
value.literal: Fang Guan, styled Cilü, was a native of Henan in Henan [commandery].

value.zh: 父融，武后時，以正諫大夫同鳳閣鸞臺平章事；
value.en: His father Rong had served under Empress Wu as Remonstrating Grand Master and associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace chancellery;
value.literal: His father Rong, during Empress Wu's reign, served as Remonstrating Grand Master and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace Chancellery;

value.zh: 神龍元年，貶死高州。
value.en: In 705 he was banished and died in exile at Gaozhou.
value.literal: In the first year of Shenlong he was demoted and died at Gaozhou.

value.zh: 琯少好學，風度沈整，以廕補弘文生。
value.en: Guan had loved scholarship from boyhood, carried himself with grave composure, and entered the Hongwen Academy by hereditary privilege.
value.literal: Guan in his youth loved learning; his bearing was grave and composed; through yin privilege he was enrolled as a Hongwen student.

value.zh: 與呂向偕隱陸渾山，十年不諧際人事。
value.en: He and Lü Xiang withdrew together to Mount Lu Hun and for ten years kept out of public life entirely.
value.literal: With Lü Xiang he retired together to Mount Lu Hun; for ten years he did not engage with worldly affairs.

value.zh: 開元中，作《封禪書》，說宰相張說，說奇之，奏為校書郎。
value.en: During the Kaiyuan era he wrote a treatise on the Feng and Shan sacrifices and showed it to Chancellor Zhang Yue, who was so impressed that he had Guan appointed collating editor.
value.literal: During Kaiyuan he composed the Fengshan shu, presented it to Chancellor Zhang Yue; Yue marveled at it and memorialized him as collating editor.

value.zh: 舉任縣令科，授盧氏令。
value.en: He passed the special examination for county magistrates and was made magistrate of Lushi.
value.literal: He passed the special examination for county magistrates and was appointed magistrate of Lushi.

value.zh: 拜監察御史，坐訊獄非是，貶睦州司戶參軍。
value.en: Appointed investigating censor, he was later demoted to revenue registrar of Muzhou for irregularities in a trial he conducted.
value.literal: He was appointed investigating censor; for errors in conducting an interrogation he was demoted to revenue registrar of Muzhou.

value.zh: 復為縣，所至上德化，興長利，以治最顯。
value.en: Restored to county office, he governed wherever he was posted with moral suasion, fostered lasting public benefit, and won renown for outstanding administration.
value.literal: Again he served as county magistrate; wherever he went he promoted virtue and transformation, developed lasting benefits, and became distinguished for the excellence of his governance.

value.zh: 俄與韋見素、崔渙奉冊靈武，見肅宗，具言上皇所以傳付意，因道當時利病，箝索虜情，辭吐華暢，帝為改容。
value.en: Shortly afterward he went with Wei Jiansu and Cui Huan to Lingwu to present the imperial register to Suzong, explained Xuanzong's purpose in abdicating, analyzed current strengths and weaknesses, and laid out the rebels' position in flowing, eloquent speech that made the emperor sit up.
value.literal: Soon with Wei Jiansu and Cui Huan he bore the registers to Lingwu, met Emperor Suzong, fully explained the Retired Emperor's intent in the transmission, and thereupon set forth the advantages and harms of the time, enumerating the enemy's situation; his words flowed with brilliance and ease, and the emperor changed expression.

value.zh: 琯既有重名。
value.en: Guan already enjoyed great fame.
value.literal: Guan already had a great reputation.

value.zh: 帝傾意待之，機務一二與琯參決，諸將相莫敢望。
value.en: The emperor leaned on him wholeheartedly, consulted him on crucial affairs, and none of the other generals or ministers could rival his standing.
value.literal: The emperor poured out his favor on him; one or two matters of state he decided together with Guan; none of the generals or chancellors dared compare.

value.zh: 於是，第五琦言財利幸，為江淮租庸使。
value.en: At this point Diwu Qi, who traded on expertise in finance, won favor and was made commissioner for Jiang-Huai tax and corvée.
value.literal: Thereupon Diwu Qi, speaking of finance and profit, won favor and became Jiang-Huai commissioner for tax and corvée.

value.zh: 琯諫曰：「往楊國忠聚斂，產怨天下。
value.en: Guan remonstrated: "Under Yang Guozhong the court squeezed revenue until the empire seethed with resentment.
value.literal: Guan remonstrated, saying: "Formerly Yang Guozhong amassed exactions and produced resentment throughout the realm.

value.zh: 陛下即位，人未見德，今又寵琦，是一國忠死，一國忠生，無以示遠方。」
value.en: You have just taken the throne and the people have yet to see benevolent rule; if you favor Qi now, it will look as though one Guozhong has died only for another to rise—how can that reassure the provinces?"
value.literal: Your Majesty has ascended the throne but the people have not yet seen virtue; now You again favor Qi—it is one Guozhong dead and another Guozhong born, with no way to show the distant regions."

value.zh: 帝曰：「六軍之命方急，無財則散。
value.en: The emperor replied: "The armies' survival hangs in the balance; without money they will scatter.
value.literal: The emperor said: "The Six Armies' fate is urgently at stake; without funds they will disperse.

value.zh: 卿惡琦可也，何所取財？」
value.en: You may dislike Qi as you please, but where else will the funds come from?"
value.literal: You may hate Qi, but where will wealth be taken from?"

value.zh: 琯不得對。
value.en: Guan had no answer.
value.literal: Guan could not reply.

value.zh: 北海太守賀蘭進明自河南至，詔攝御史大夫、嶺南節度使，入謝，帝曰：「朕語琯除正大夫，何為攝邪？」
value.en: Helan Jinming, prefect of Beihai, arrived from Henan and was ordered to serve as acting censor-in-chief and military commissioner of Lingnan. When he came to give thanks, the emperor said, "I told Guan to appoint you full censor-in-chief—why 'acting'?"
value.literal: Beihai prefect Helan Jinming came from Henan; he was ordered as acting censor-in-chief and Lingnan military commissioner; entering to give thanks, the emperor said: "We told Guan to appoint you full grand master—why 'acting'?"

value.zh: 進明銜之，因曰：「陛下知晉亂乎？
value.en: Jinming took offense and said, "Does Your Majesty know how the Jin dynasty was ruined?
value.literal: Jinming bore a grudge over this and thereupon said: "Does Your Majesty know how Jin fell into disorder?

value.zh: 惟以尚虛名，任王衍為宰相，基祖浮華，不事天下事，故至於敗。
value.en: They prized empty reputation, put Wang Yan in the chancellery, and built policy on showy refinement while neglecting the realm—until the state collapsed.
value.literal: It was solely because they valued empty reputation, employed Wang Yan as chancellor, who founded his lineage in frivolity and ornament and did not attend to the realm's affairs, and therefore came to defeat.

value.zh: 方唐中興，當用實才，而琯性疏闊，大言無當，非宰相器。
value.en: Tang is trying to revive itself and needs practical men, but Guan is scatterbrained, full of empty talk, and unfit for the chancellery.
value.literal: Now as Tang is reviving, solid talent should be employed; yet Guan's nature is broad and loose, his grand words ineffectual—he is not material for chancellor.

value.zh: 陛下待之厚，然孰肯為陛下用乎？」
value.en: You treat him generously, but who under him would truly serve you?"
value.literal: Your Majesty treats him generously, yet who would be willing to serve Your Majesty for his sake?"

value.zh: 帝曰：「何哉？」
value.en: The emperor asked, "How so?"
value.literal: The emperor said: "How so?"

value.zh: 對曰：「陛下頃為皇太子，太子出曰撫軍，入曰監國，而琯為聖皇建遣諸王為都統節度，乃謂陛下為元子而付以朔方、河東、河北空虛之地，永王、豐王乃統四節度。
value.en: He replied: "When you were crown prince, a prince leaving court was styled 'military overseer' and returning 'regent of the realm.' Yet Guan, acting for the retired emperor, had the princes made overall commanders and military commissioners: he treated you as eldest son but gave you the depleted territories of Shuofang, Hedong, and Hebei, while Princes Yong and Feng held four military commissions between them.
value.literal: He replied: "When Your Majesty was still crown prince, the prince going out was styled 'military governor' and coming in 'regent of the realm,' yet Guan, for the Retired Emperor, devised sending the princes as overall commanders and military commissioners, and thereby treated Your Majesty as eldest son while assigning You the empty territories of Shuofang, Hedong, and Hebei, while Prince Yong and Prince Feng commanded four military commissions.

value.zh: 此於聖皇似忠，于陛下非忠也。
value.en: That looked loyal to the retired emperor but was not loyal to you.
value.literal: This toward the Retired Emperor seems loyal, but toward Your Majesty it is not loyal.

value.zh: 琯意諸子一得天下，身不失恩，又多樹私黨，以副戎權，推此而言，豈肯盡誠于陛下乎？」
value.en: Guan meant that whichever prince won the throne, he would keep his own favor; he also built private factions to back military power. On that logic, would he ever serve you with whole-hearted loyalty?"
value.literal: Guan's intent was that whichever son gained the realm, he himself would not lose favor; moreover he planted many private factions to support military power—pursuing this reasoning, how could he be willing to devote full loyalty to Your Majesty?"

value.zh: 帝入其語，始惡琯。
value.en: The emperor accepted this account and began to turn against Guan.
value.literal: The emperor took in his words and began to dislike Guan.

value.zh: 以進明為御史大夫、河南節度使。
value.en: Jinming was made censor-in-chief and military commissioner of Henan.
value.literal: Jinming was appointed censor-in-chief and Henan military commissioner.

value.zh: 華溫琪
value.en: Hua Wenqi
value.literal: Hua Wenqi

value.zh: 筠弟抃，當筠為京兆尹時，以為牙內指揮使、三白渠營田制置使。
value.en: Yun’s younger brother Bian, while Yun was governor of Jingzhao, was made commander of the inner guard and commissioner for the Three White Canal colonies.
value.literal: Yun’s younger brother Bian, when Yun was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, was made commander of the inner guard and commissioner for the Three White Canal military colonies.

value.zh: 筠西伐蜀，留抃守京兆。
value.en: Yun marched west against Shu and left Bian to hold Jingzhao.
value.literal: When Yun campaigned west against Shu he left Bian to hold Jingzhao.

value.zh: 蜀平，魏王繼岌班師，至興平，而明宗自魏起，京師大亂，抃乃斷咸陽浮橋以拒繼岌，繼岌乃自殺。
value.en: Shu pacified, Prince of Wei Jiji withdrew. At Xingping Mingzong rose from Wei and the capital erupted. Bian cut the Xianyang floating bridge to block Jiji; Jiji killed himself.
value.literal: When Shu was pacified the Prince of Wei Jiji withdrew the army; reaching Xingping, Mingzong rose from Wei and the capital fell into great disorder; Bian then cut the Xianyang floating bridge to block Jiji, and Jiji thereupon killed himself.

value.zh: 初，筠代康懷英為永平軍節度使，而懷英死，筠即掠其家貲。
value.en: When Yun replaced Kang Huaiying as commissioner of Yongping and Huaiying died, Yun looted his household at once.
value.literal: Earlier, when Yun replaced Kang Huaiying as military commissioner of Yongping and Huaiying died, Yun at once plundered his household goods.

value.zh: 又於唐故宮掘地，多得金玉。
value.en: He dug in the old Tang palace grounds and found much gold and jade.
value.literal: He also dug in the ground of the old Tang palace and obtained much gold and jade.

value.zh: 有偏將侯莫陳威者，嘗與溫韜發唐諸陵，分得寶貨，筠因以事殺威而取之。
value.en: Deputy Hou Mo Chenwei had once joined Wen Tao in opening the Tang tombs and splitting the treasure. Yun killed him on that pretext and took the hoard.
value.literal: There was a deputy general Hou Mo Chenwei who had once with Wen Tao opened the Tang tombs and divided the treasures; Yun on that account killed Wei and took them.

value.zh: 魏王繼岌死渭南，抃悉取其行橐。
value.en: When Prince of Wei Jiji died at Weinan, Bian seized all his traveling baggage.
value.literal: When Prince of Wei Jiji died at Weinan, Bian took all his traveling baggage.

value.zh: 而王衍自蜀行至秦川，莊宗遣宦者向延嗣殺之，延嗣因盡得衍蜀中珍寶。
value.en: Wang Yan of Shu was marched toward Qinchuan when Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to kill him; Yansi took all Yan’s Shu treasures.
value.literal: Wang Yan of Shu was being escorted to Qinchuan when Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to kill him; Yansi thereby obtained all of Yan’s Shu treasures.

value.zh: 明宗即位，即遣人捕誅宦者，延嗣亡命，而蜀之珍寶抃又取之。
value.en: Mingzong took the throne and sent men to hunt down the eunuchs. Yansi fled; Bian took the Shu treasures again.
value.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he at once sent men to seize and execute the eunuchs; Yansi fled, and Bian again took the Shu treasures.

value.zh: 由是兄弟貲皆巨萬。
value.en: The brothers’ wealth each ran to tens of millions.
value.literal: Thereby the brothers’ wealth each reached tens of millions.

value.zh: 然筠為人好施予，以其富，故所至不為聚斂，民賴以安。
value.en: Yun loved to give. Rich as he was, he did not squeeze the people wherever he served, and they lived easier for it.
value.literal: Yet Yun as a man loved to give; because he was wealthy, wherever he went he did not practice heavy exactions, and the people relied on him for peace.

value.zh: 而抃嗜酒貪鄙，歷沂、密二州刺史。
value.en: Bian drank hard, was greedy and base, and held Yi and Mi.
value.literal: Bian was addicted to wine, greedy, and base, and served as prefect of Yi and Mi prefectures.

value.zh: 晉出帝時，以將軍市馬於回鶻，坐馬不中式，有司理其價直，抃性鄙，因郁郁而卒。
value.en: Under Jin’s Outgoing Emperor he went as a general to buy horses from the Uyghurs. The horses failed inspection; the authorities charged him the price. Mean by nature, he sickened and died of spite.
value.literal: Under Jin’s Outgoing Emperor he went as a general to buy horses from the Uyghurs; because the horses did not meet standard, the authorities assessed their value; Bian’s nature was base, and he therefore died in gloom.

value.zh: 《傳》曰：「禮義廉恥，國之四維；
value.en: A commentary says: "Ritual, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame are the four pillars of the state;
value.literal: A commentary says: "Ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame are the four bonds of a state;

value.zh: 四維不張，國乃滅亡。」
value.en: if these four pillars are not upheld, the state will be destroyed."
value.literal: if the four bonds are not extended, the state will perish.

value.zh: 善乎，管生之能言也！
value.en: Well said indeed—how aptly Master Guan put it!
value.literal: How well said—Master Guan's power of expression!

value.zh: 禮義，治人之大法；
value.en: Ritual and righteousness are the great principles by which men are governed;
value.literal: Ritual and righteousness are the great laws for governing people;

value.zh: 廉恥，立人之大節。
value.en: integrity and shame are the great standards by which a person stands upright.
value.literal: integrity and shame are the great standards for establishing a person.

value.zh: 蓋不廉，則無所不取；
value.en: Without integrity, a man will seize anything;
value.literal: For if one lacks integrity, there is nothing he will not seize;

value.zh: 不恥，則無所不為。
value.en: without shame, he will stoop to anything.
value.literal: if one lacks shame, there is nothing he will not do.

value.zh: 人而如此，則禍亂敗亡，亦無所不至，況為大臣而無所不取，無所不為，則天下其有不亂，國家其有不亡者乎！
value.en: When ordinary men behave this way, disaster and ruin follow without limit; when great ministers seize anything and stoop to anything, how can the realm remain at peace or the state escape destruction?
value.literal: When a man is like this, calamity, disorder, ruin, and destruction know no limit; how much more when a great minister will seize anything and do anything—can the realm fail to fall into chaos, or the state fail to perish!

value.zh: 予讀馮道《長樂老敘》，見其自述以為榮，其可謂無廉恥者矣，則天下國家可從而知也。
value.en: When I read Feng Dao's Account of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy and saw him boast of his own career, I knew him for a man utterly devoid of integrity and shame—and from that one may infer the fate of realm and state.
value.literal: When I read Feng Dao's "Account of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy," I saw that he took pride in his own account of himself; one may say he had no integrity or shame, and from this the realm and the state may be understood.

value.zh: 唐莊宗滅梁，愚朝京師，唐諸公卿素聞愚學古，重之，拜主客郎中、翰林學士。
value.en: When Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang, Yu attended court at the capital. Tang officials had long heard of Yu's classical learning and held him in esteem; he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Receptions and Hanlin Academician.
value.literal: When Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang, Yu attended court at the capital. Tang officials had long heard of Yu's classical learning and held him in esteem; he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Receptions and Hanlin Academician.

value.zh: 魏王繼岌伐蜀，辟愚都統判官。
value.en: When the Prince of Wei, Jiji, marched against Shu, he recruited Yu as aide to the overall commander.
value.literal: When the Prince of Wei, Jiji, marched against Shu, he recruited Yu as aide to the overall commander.

value.zh: 蜀道阻險，議者以謂宜緩師待變而進，招討使郭崇韜以決於愚，愚曰：「王衍荒怠，亂國之政，其人厭之。
value.en: The roads into Shu were perilous and obstructed. Those debating the matter said the army ought to advance slowly and wait for changes; campaign commissioner Guo Chongtao sought Yu's decision. Yu said, "Wang Yan is negligent and dissolute, his government ruining the state, and the people revile him.
value.literal: The roads into Shu were perilous and obstructed. Those debating the matter said the army ought to advance slowly and wait for changes; the campaign commissioner Guo Chongtao sought Yu's decision. Yu said: "Wang Yan is negligent and dissolute, his rule ruining the state—the people revile him.

value.zh: 乘其倉卒，擊其無備，其利在速，不可緩也。」
value.en: Seize their unpreparedness in haste—strike while they are off guard. The advantage lies in speed; we must not delay."
value.literal: Seize their unpreparedness in haste—the advantage lies in speed; we must not delay.

value.zh: 崇韜以為然，而所至迎降，遂以滅蜀。
value.en: Chongtao agreed. Wherever they went they were met with surrender, and thus Shu was destroyed.
value.literal: Chongtao agreed; wherever they went they were met with surrender, and thus Shu was destroyed.

value.zh: 初，軍行至寶雞，招討判官陳乂稱疾請留，愚厲聲曰：「陳乂見利則進，知難則止。
value.en: At first, when the army reached Baoji, campaign aide Chen Yi pleaded illness and asked to remain behind. Yu said in a stern voice, "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he knows difficulty.
value.literal: At first, when the army reached Baoji, the campaign aide Chen Yi pleaded illness and asked to remain behind. Yu said in a stern voice: "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he knows difficulty.

value.zh: 今大軍涉險，人心易搖，正可斬之以徇。」
value.en: Now the great army crosses dangerous ground and hearts are easily shaken—this is precisely when he should be beheaded to make an example."
value.literal: Now the great army crosses dangerous ground and hearts are easily shaken—this is precisely when he should be beheaded to make an example.

value.zh: 由是軍中無敢言留者。
value.en: From that point on, none in the army dared speak of remaining behind.
value.literal: From this, none in the army dared speak of remaining behind.

value.zh: 奚 吐渾 達靼 党項 突厥 吐蕃 回鶻 于闐 高麗 渤海 新羅 黑水靺鞨 南詔蠻 牂牁 昆明 占城
value.en: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Turks, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Khotan, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Mohe, Nanzhao, Zhangke, Kunming, and Champa.
value.literal: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Turk, Tibet, Uyghur, Khotan, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Mohe, Nanzhao, Zhangke, Kunming, Champa.

value.zh: 同光三年，魏王繼岌及郭崇韜等破蜀，得王衍時所俘南詔蠻數十人，又得徐藹，自言嘗使南詔，乃矯詔還其所俘，遣藹等持金帛招撫南詔，諭以威德，南詔不納。
value.en: In the third year of Tongguang Prince Jiji of Wei and Guo Chongtao conquered Shu, recovered dozens of Nanzhao captives taken under Wang Yan, and found Xu Ai, who claimed prior service as envoy. They forged an edict returning the captives and sent Ai with gold and silk to win Nanzhao over—but Nanzhao refused.
value.literal: In the third year of Tongguang Prince of Wei Jiji and Guo Chongtao and others defeated Shu, obtained several dozen Nanzhao captives from Wang Yan's time, and also Xu Ai, who said he had once been envoy to Nanzhao; they forged an edict to return the captives and sent Ai and others with gold and silk to win over Nanzhao, instructing them in power and virtue—Nanzhao did not accept.

value.zh: 至明宗時，巂州山后兩林百蠻都鬼主、右武衛大將軍李卑晚，遣大鬼主傅能何華來朝貢，明宗拜卑晚甯遠將軍，又以大渡河南山前邛州六姓都鬼主懷安郡王勿定摽莎爲定遠將軍。
value.en: Under Mingzong, Li Beiwan, paramount lord of the Two Forests tribes behind Xizhou and a Right Martial Guard general, sent the great ghost lord Fu Nenghua with tribute. Mingzong made Beiwan a General Who Pacifies the Distance and appointed Wuding Biaosha of the Six Clans south of the Dadu River a General Who Fixes the Distance.
value.literal: By Mingzong's time the Xizhou mountain rear Two Forests Hundred Barbarians paramount ghost lord and Right Martial Guard senior general Li Beiwan sent the great ghost lord Fu Nenghua to pay tribute; Mingzong appointed Beiwan General Who Pacifies the Distance, and also made the Qiongzhou Six Clans paramount ghost lord south of the Dadu River, Prince of Huai'an Wuding Biaosha, General Who Fixes the Distance.

value.zh: 明年遣左金吾衛將軍烏昭遠爲入蠻國信使，昭遠不能達而還。
value.en: The next year Left Golden Crow Guard general Wu Zhaoyuan was sent as envoy to the barbarian lands but could not get through and returned.
value.literal: The next year they sent Left Golden Crow Guard general Wu Zhaoyuan as credentialed envoy into the barbarian state; Zhaoyuan could not reach it and returned.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

value.zh: 有司奏：「尚書令王衍備位大臣，太子被誣，志在苟免，請禁錮終身。」
value.en: Authorities memorialized: "Wang Yan, having held high office, sought only to save himself when the heir apparent was framed, and asked lifelong ban from office."
value.literal: The authorities memorialized: "Wang Yan, Director of the Masters of Writing, occupied a minister's post; when the Heir Apparent was falsely accused his aim was only to escape harm—request lifelong prohibition from office."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: Granted.
value.literal: It was granted.

value.zh: 資治通鑑 第154卷
value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 154
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 154

value.zh: 爾朱仲遠攻西兗州，丁丑，拔之，擒刺史王衍。
value.en: Erzhu Zhongyuan attacked Western Yanzhou. On dingchou he captured it and seized Inspector Wang Yan.
value.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan attacked Western Yanzhou. On dingchou he took it and captured the inspector Wang Yan.

value.zh: 衍，蕭之兄子也。
value.en: Yan was the son of Xiao's elder brother.
value.literal: Yan was a nephew of Xiao by his elder brother.

value.zh: 癸未，敬宗以右衛將軍賀拔勝為東征都督。
value.en: On guiwei Emperor Xiaozhuang made Right Guard General Heba Sheng commander of the eastern campaign.
value.literal: On guiwei Jingzong appointed Right Guard General Heba Sheng eastern campaign commander-in-chief.

value.zh: 壬辰，又以鄭先護兼尚書左僕射為行台，與勝共討仲遠。
value.en: On renchen he also named Zheng Xianhu, who concurrently served as left vice director of the secretariat, mobile headquarters commissioner, to join Sheng against Zhongyuan.
value.literal: On renchen he also made Zheng Xianhu, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, mobile headquarters commissioner, to join Sheng in attacking Zhongyuan.

value.zh: 戊戌，詔罷魏蘭根行台，以定州刺史薛曇尚兼尚書，為北道行台。
value.en: On wuxu an edict dissolved Wei Langen's mobile headquarters and made Dingzhou inspector Xue Tanshang, concurrently a secretariat director, northern-route mobile headquarters commissioner.
value.literal: On wuxu an edict abolished Wei Langen's mobile headquarters and made Dingzhou Inspector Xue Tanshang, concurrently Director of the Secretariat, northern-route mobile headquarters commissioner.

value.zh: 鄭先護疑賀拔勝，置之營外。
value.en: Zheng Xianhu distrusted Heba Sheng and posted him outside the camp.
value.literal: Zheng Xianhu distrusted Heba Sheng and kept him outside the camp.

value.zh: 庚子，勝與仲遠戰於滑台東，兵敗，降於仲遠。
value.en: On gengzi Sheng met Zhongyuan east of Huatai, lost, and surrendered to him.
value.literal: On gengzi Sheng fought Zhongyuan east of Huatai, was defeated, and surrendered to Zhongyuan.

value.zh: 資治通鑑巻第二百一十四
value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214

value.zh: 張守珪使平盧討撃使、左驍衞將軍安祿山討奚、契丹叛者，祿山恃勇輕進，爲虜所敗。
value.en: Zhang Shougui sent Pinglu Strike Commissioner and Left Brave Guard General An Lushan against Xi and Khitan rebels; Lushan, overconfident, advanced rashly and was defeated.
value.literal: Zhang Shougui sent Pinglu Strike Commissioner and Left Brave Guard General An Lushan to attack Xi and Khitan rebels; Lushan, relying on his courage, advanced rashly and was defeated by the enemy.

value.zh: 夏，四月，辛亥，守珪奏請斬之。
value.en: In summer, the fourth month, on xinhai, Shougui memorialized asking that he be executed.
value.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinhai, Shougui memorialized requesting his execution.

value.zh: 祿山臨刑呼曰：「大夫不欲滅奚、契丹邪！
value.en: Facing execution, Lushan cried: "Commissioner, do you not wish to destroy the Xi and Khitan!
value.literal: As Lushan faced execution he cried: "Commissioner, do you not wish to destroy the Xi and Khitan!

value.zh: 奈何殺祿山！」
value.en: Why kill Lushan!"
value.literal: Why kill Lushan!"

value.zh: 守珪亦惜其驍勇，欲活之，乃更執送京師。
value.en: Shougui, valuing his fighting skill, wished to spare him and sent him to the capital under guard instead.
value.literal: Shougui also prized his fierce valor and wished to spare him, and so bound him and sent him to the capital.

value.zh: 張九齡批曰：「昔穰苴誅莊賈，孫武斬宮嬪。
value.en: Zhang Jiuling wrote in the margin: "Long ago Rang Ju executed Zhuang Jia and Sun Wu beheaded palace women.
value.literal: Zhang Jiuling annotated: "In the past Rang Ju executed Zhuang Jia and Sun Wu beheaded palace women.

value.zh: 守珪軍令若行，祿山不宜免死。」
value.en: If Shougui enforced military law, Lushan should not have been spared."
value.literal: If Shougui's military law were enforced, Lushan ought not to escape death."

value.zh: 上惜其才，敕令免官，以白衣將領。
value.en: The Emperor prized his talent, pardoned him from office, and let him lead troops in plain clothes.
value.literal: The Emperor prized his talent and ordered him pardoned from office, to lead troops as a commoner.

value.zh: 九齡固爭曰：「祿山失律喪師，於法不可不誅。
value.en: Jiuling insisted: "Lushan broke discipline and lost his army; by law he must die.
value.literal: Jiuling firmly remonstrated: "Lushan violated discipline and lost the army; by law he cannot go unpunished.

value.zh: 且臣觀其貌有反相，不殺必爲後患。」
value.en: Moreover I see rebel features in his face; if he is not killed he will become a future scourge."
value.literal: Moreover I observe that his appearance has the look of a rebel; if he is not killed he will surely become a later trouble."

value.zh: 上曰：「卿勿以王夷甫識石勒，枉害忠良。」
value.en: The Emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yifu mistaking Shi Le, wrongly destroy a loyal man."
value.literal: The Emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yifu recognizing Shi Le, wrongly harm a loyal man."

value.zh: 竟赦之。
value.en: In the end he was pardoned.
value.literal: In the end he was pardoned.
